Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 1–2:

Tafsir of Surat al-Furqan

It is a Meccan surah. In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

* *

Allah, the Exalted, praises Himself for having sent down to His noble Messenger the Great Qur'an, as He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, who has sent down to His servant the Book and has not made therein any deviance. [He made it] straight, to warn of severe punishment from Him and to give good tidings to the believers who do righteous deeds that they will have a good reward, abiding therein forever.﴾ [al-Kahf: 1-3]. Here He said: ﴿Blessed is He﴾, and tabaraka is from tafa'ul (reciprocal form) of al-barakah (blessing), which is established, lasting and enduring. ﴿He who sent down the Furqan﴾. Nazzala is fa''ala, from repetition and multiplicity, as He said: ﴿And the Book which He sent down to His Messenger and the Book which He sent down before﴾ [an-Nisa: 136]. This is because the earlier scriptures used to be sent down all at once, whereas the Qur'an was sent down in installments, separated, detailed, verse after verse, rulings after rulings, and surah after surah. This is stronger and more eloquent, and shows greater care for the one to whom it was sent, as He said in the middle of this surah: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?" Thus [it is], that We may strengthen thereby your heart; and We have spaced it out distinctly. And they do not come to you with an example except that We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ [al-Furqan: 32-33]. For this reason He named it here al-Furqan, because it distinguishes between truth and falsehood, guidance and misguidance, error and right conduct, and the lawful and the unlawful.

* *

His saying ﴿His servant﴾ is an attribute of praise and commendation, because He attributed him to His servitude, just as He described him with it in his most honourable state, which was the night of the Isra', when He said: ﴿Glory be to the One who took His servant by night﴾ [al-Isra: 1]. And just as He described him with it in the station of calling to Him: ﴿And when the servant of Allah stood up calling upon Him, they nearly became a mass crowding against him﴾ [al-Jinn: 19]. Likewise He described him with it at the time of the sending down of the Book to him and the descent of the angel to him, saying: ﴿Blessed is He who sent down the Furqan upon His servant, that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾.

* *

His saying ﴿that he may be a warner to the worlds﴾ means: He specifically singled him out with this Great, Clear, Detailed, Firm Book, in which ﴿falsehood cannot approach it from before it or behind it; [it is] a revelation from the All-Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42], which He made a great Furqan. He singled him out with it so that He would specifically entrust him with the message to those who shade themselves under the green (sky) and stand firmly upon the dust (earth). As he said, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: "I have been sent to the red and the black" [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. 521, and the one following it, from the hadith of Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him]. He also said: "I have been given five things which none of the prophets before me were given," and he mentioned among them: "A prophet used to be sent only to his own people, but I have been sent to all people." Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: O mankind, indeed I am the Messenger of Allah to you all, [the Messenger of] He to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. There is no deity except Him; He gives life and causes death﴾ [al-A'raf: 158]. That is: the One who sent me is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, who says to a thing "Be," and it is; He is the One who gives life and causes death. Likewise He said here: ﴿to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and who has not taken a son, and has no partner in dominion﴾, so He declared Himself free of having a son and of having a partner.

Then He informed that He: ﴿created everything and determined it with precise determination﴾, meaning: everything other than Him is created and sustained; He is the Creator of everything, its Lord, its Sovereign and its God, and everything is under His subjugation [and subjection], His management and His decree [and His control, His subjection, His management].

The Most High informs us of the ignorance of the polytheists in taking deities besides Allah, the Creator of everything, the Possessor of the reins of all affairs, who, whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be. Despite this, they worshipped alongside Him idols that have no power to create even the wing of a gnat. Rather, they themselves are created, and they possess neither harm nor benefit for themselves, so how could they possess anything for those who worship them? ﴿And they possess neither death nor life nor resurrection﴾, meaning that they have no share in any of that. Rather, all of that is referred back entirely to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, who gives life and causes death, and who will restore all creatures on the Day of Resurrection, the first of them and the last of them. ﴿Your creation and your resurrection are only like that of a single soul﴾ [Luqman: 28]. ﴿And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye﴾ [al-Qamar: 50]. ﴿It will be but a single blast, and at once they will be on the surface of the earth﴾ [al-Nazi'at: 13-14]. ﴿It will be but a single shout, and at once they will be looking on﴾ [al-Saffat: 19]. ﴿It will be but a single shout, and at once they will all be brought before Us﴾ [Ya-Sin: 53]. So He is Allah, there is no god besides Him and no lord other than Him, and worship is not fitting except for Him, because whatever He wills comes to be and whatever He does not will does not come to be. He is the One who has no child and no parent, and no equal, no rival, no minister and no like. Rather, He is the One, the Eternal Refuge (al-Samad), who has not begotten and has not been begotten, and there is none comparable to Him.

Allah says, informing about the feebleness of the minds of the ignorant among the disbelievers, in their saying about the Qur'an: ﴿This is nothing but a lie﴾, i.e., falsehood, ﴿which he (Muhammad)[[In Fa and A: "Muhammad".]] has fabricated﴾ — meaning the Prophet ﷺ — ﴿and others have helped him with it﴾, i.e., he sought help in composing it from other people. Allah says: ﴿They have committed injustice and falsehood﴾, i.e., they have fabricated a false statement which they know to be false, and they know the lie of their own claims, in what they allege.

﴿And they say, "Tales of the ancients, which he has had written down, and they are dictated to him morning and evening."﴾ Meaning: the books of the ancients, which he had copied. ﴿So they are dictated to him﴾, i.e., they are read to him ﴿morning and evening﴾, i.e., at the beginning and end of the day.

This statement — given its feebleness, its falsehood, and their slander — is known to be false by everyone, for it has been established by mass transmission (tawatur) and by necessity that Muhammad, the Messenger of Allah, did not practise any writing at all, neither at the beginning of his life nor at its end. He grew up among them from the time of his birth until Allah sent him, about forty years, and they knew his comings and goings, his truthfulness, his righteousness, his trustworthiness, and that he was free from lying, immorality and all base characteristics. Indeed, during his youth until he was sent, they did not call him anything but "al-Amin" (the Trustworthy), because of what they knew of his truthfulness and righteousness. When Allah honoured him with what He honoured him with, they set up enmity against him and accused him of these statements, from which every sensible person knows he is innocent, and they were bewildered as to what to charge him with. Sometimes, out of their falsehood, they say, "He is a sorcerer"; sometimes they say, "He is a poet"; sometimes they say, "He is mad"; and sometimes they say, "He is a liar." Allah says: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you; so they have gone astray and cannot find a way﴾ [al-Isra': 48].

And Allah says, in answer to what they opposed and fabricated here: ﴿Say: "It has been sent down by He who knows the secret in the heavens and the earth."﴾ I.e., He has sent down the Qur'an, which contains the reports of the former and latter peoples, as a true and truthful report, conforming to the reality outside, past and future. ﴿He who knows the secret﴾ — i.e., Allah, who knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and knows the hidden things as He knows the apparent ones.

* *

His saying: ﴿Indeed He is ever Forgiving, Merciful﴾ is a call to them to repentance and turning back, and an information that His mercy is vast, His forbearance great, and whoever turns to Him, He will turn towards him. Despite their lying, fabrication, immorality, slander, disbelief and obstinacy, and what they said about the Messenger and the Qur'an, He calls them to repentance and to abandon what they are in, and to Islam and guidance, as He says: ﴿Certainly those who say, "Indeed Allah is the third of three," have disbelieved, and there is no god except One God. And if they do not desist from what they say, there will surely afflict those who disbelieve among them a painful punishment. * Will they not repent to Allah and seek His forgiveness? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 73–74]. And He says: ﴿Indeed, those who have tormented the believing men and believing women and then have not repented – for them is the punishment of Hell, and for them is the punishment of the Burning﴾ [al-Buruj: 10]. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: "Look at this generosity and munificence: they killed His friends, and He calls them to repentance and mercy [glorified and exalted is He]."

Allah the Exalted informs of the obstinacy, stubbornness and denial of the truth by the disbelievers, without any proof or evidence from them. They only offered excuses by saying: ﴿What is this Messenger that he eats food﴾, meaning: just as we eat it and need it as we need it; ﴿and walks in the markets﴾, that is, goes back and forth in them seeking gain and trade; ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he could be a warner with him?﴾ They say: Why was an angel not sent down to him from Allah, to be a witness for him to the truth of what he claims! This is like what Pharaoh said: ﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed on him, or why have the angels not come with him in procession?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 53]. Likewise these people said the same, their hearts being alike. Therefore He said: ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him﴾, that is, the knowledge of a treasure [being] from which he could spend; ﴿or he have a garden from which he eats﴾, that is, one that moves with him wherever he goes. All of this is easy and simple for Allah, but for Him there is wisdom in leaving it, and for Him is the conclusive proof. ﴿And the wrongdoers said: You follow only a man affected by sorcery.﴾

Allah says: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you﴾, that is, they bring forth what they hurl at you and lie about you with, from their saying "a sorcerer, one affected by sorcery, a madman, a liar, a poet." All of these are false statements; everyone who has even a little understanding and intellect knows their lying and fabrication in this. Therefore He said: ﴿so they have gone astray﴾, that is, from the path of guidance, ﴿and they cannot find a way﴾. This is because whoever departs from the truth is astray wherever he turns, for the truth is one and its method is unified, each part confirming the others.

Then Allah the Exalted said, informing His Prophet that if He willed, He would give him better than what they say in this world, and finer and superior: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾

Mujahid said: this means in this world. He said: The Quraysh call every house of stone a palace, whether it is large or small.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Khaythama: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If you wish, we will give you the treasures of the earth and its keys, which no prophet before you was given, and none after you will be given, and that will not diminish what you have with Allah?" He said: "Gather them for me in the Hereafter." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning that: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/140) through Sufyan, as a mursal report.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿Rather, they deny the Hour﴾, that is: these people only say such things out of denial and obstinacy, not because they seek insight and guidance; rather, their denial of the Day of Resurrection drives them to say these statements they make. ﴿And We have prepared﴾, that is, and We have readied ﴿for those who deny the Hour a blazing fire (sa'ir)﴾, that is, a painful torment, intensely hot and unbearable, in the Fire of Hell.

Al-Thawri said, from Salama ibn Kuhayl, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr: "Sa'ir" is a valley of the pus of Hell.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾, that is, Hell sees them ﴿from a distant place﴾, meaning: at the place of gathering. Al-Suddi said: from a distance of a hundred years. ﴿They will hear its raging and roaring﴾, that is, rage against them, as Allah says: ﴿When they are thrown into it, they will hear its roaring while it boils, almost bursting with fury﴾ [Al-Mulk: 7-8], meaning: it almost splits apart from one another out of its intense fury against those who disbelieved in Allah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Idris ibn Hatim ibn al-Akhyaf al-Wasiti narrated to us that he heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wasiti, from Asbagh ibn Zayd, from Khalid ibn Kathir, from Khalid ibn Durayk, from a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says about me what I did not say, or claims to a father other than his own, or attributes himself to other than his clients, let him take his seat in the Fire." And in another narration: "Let him take a seat between the two eyes of Hell." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, does it have two eyes? He said: "Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾..." the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Khidash, from Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti, with it.

He also said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Sulaym, from Abu Wa'il, who said: We went out with 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud), and with us was al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym. They passed by a blacksmith, and 'Abd Allah stood looking at a piece of iron in the fire, and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym looked at it too and swayed as if about to fall. Then 'Abd Allah passed by a kiln on the bank of the Euphrates, and when he saw it with the fire blazing within it, he recited this verse: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾, and al-Rabi' (i.e., Ibn Khuthaym) fainted. They carried him to his household, and 'Abd Allah stayed with him until noon, but he did not revive. May Allah be pleased with him.

And my father narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Indeed the servant is dragged towards the Fire, and it neighs at him like a mule neighing for barley, then it exhales an exhalation such that no one remains but fears.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in abridged form like this, and Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated it fully:

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and it shrinks and draws its parts together, and the Most Merciful says to it: "What is wrong with you?" It says: "He seeks refuge from me." He says: "Release My servant." And indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and he says: "O Lord, is this how I thought of You?" He says: "And what was your thought?" He says: "That Your mercy would encompass me." He says: "Release My servant." And indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and it neighs at him like a mule neighing for barley, and it exhales an exhalation such that no one remains but fears. This is a sound chain.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, regarding His saying: ﴿they will hear its raging and roaring﴾, he said: Indeed Hell exhales an exhalation, and no king or prophet remains but falls trembling at the knees, until Abraham, peace be upon him, kneels on his knees and says: "My Lord, today I ask of You only for myself." [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/56).]

As for His saying: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾, that is, Hell sees them ﴿from a distant place﴾, meaning: at the place of gathering. Al-Suddi said: from a distance of a hundred years. ﴿They will hear its raging and roaring﴾, that is, rage against them, as Allah says: ﴿When they are thrown into it, they will hear its roaring while it boils, almost bursting with fury﴾ [Al-Mulk: 7-8], meaning: it almost splits apart from one another out of its intense fury against those who disbelieved in Allah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Idris ibn Hatim ibn al-Akhyaf al-Wasiti narrated to us that he heard Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Wasiti, from Asbagh ibn Zayd, from Khalid ibn Kathir, from Khalid ibn Durayk, from a man among the companions of the Prophet ﷺ, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever says about me what I did not say, or claims to a father other than his own, or attributes himself to other than his clients, let him take his seat in the Fire." And in another narration: "Let him take a seat between the two eyes of Hell." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, does it have two eyes? He said: "Have you not heard Allah say: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place﴾..." the verse.

Ibn Jarir narrated it from Muhammad ibn Khidash, from Muhammad ibn Yazid al-Wasiti, with it.

He also said: My father narrated to us, 'Ali ibn Muhammad al-Tanafisi narrated to us, Abu Bakr ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from 'Isa ibn Sulaym, from Abu Wa'il, who said: We went out with 'Abd Allah (i.e., Ibn Mas'ud), and with us was al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym. They passed by a blacksmith, and 'Abd Allah stood looking at a piece of iron in the fire, and al-Rabi' ibn Khuthaym looked at it too and swayed as if about to fall. Then 'Abd Allah passed by a kiln on the bank of the Euphrates, and when he saw it with the fire blazing within it, he recited this verse: ﴿When it sees them from a distant place, they will hear its raging and roaring﴾, and al-Rabi' (i.e., Ibn Khuthaym) fainted. They carried him to his household, and 'Abd Allah stayed with him until noon, but he did not revive. May Allah be pleased with him.

And my father narrated to us: 'Abd Allah ibn Raja' narrated to us, Isra'il narrated to us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Indeed the servant is dragged towards the Fire, and it neighs at him like a mule neighing for barley, then it exhales an exhalation such that no one remains but fears.

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in abridged form like this, and Imam Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir narrated it fully:

Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Dawraqi narrated to us, 'Ubayd Allah ibn Musa narrated to us, Isra'il informed us, from Abu Yahya, from Mujahid, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: Indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and it shrinks and draws its parts together, and the Most Merciful says to it: "What is wrong with you?" It says: "He seeks refuge from me." He says: "Release My servant." And indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and he says: "O Lord, is this how I thought of You?" He says: "And what was your thought?" He says: "That Your mercy would encompass me." He says: "Release My servant." And indeed the man is dragged towards the Fire, and it neighs at him like a mule neighing for barley, and it exhales an exhalation such that no one remains but fears. This is a sound chain.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Mansur, from Mujahid, from 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, regarding His saying: ﴿they will hear its raging and roaring﴾, he said: Indeed Hell exhales an exhalation, and no king or prophet remains but falls trembling at the knees, until Abraham, peace be upon him, kneels on his knees and says: "My Lord, today I ask of You only for myself." [Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/56).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it﴾, Qatadah said, from Abu Ayyub, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: like the point of a spear, that is, because of its narrowness.

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Nafi' ibn Yazid informed me, from Yahya ibn Abi Usayd, who raised the report to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he was asked about the saying of Allah: ﴿And when they are cast into a narrow place of it, bound together﴾, and he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, they will be forced into the Fire as a peg is forced into a wall." [Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/240).]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿bound together (muqarranin)﴾, Abu Salih said: meaning, bound with their hands tied. ﴿There they will call out for destruction (thubur)﴾, that is, with woe, regret and loss. ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.﴾ Imam Ahmad said: 'Affan narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first to be clothed in a garment of Fire will be Iblis; he will place it upon his eyebrows and drag it behind him, and his offspring after him, and he will cry out: 'Woe to me!' and they will cry out: 'Woe to them!' until they stand at the Fire, and he says: 'Woe to me!' and they say: 'Woe to them!' Then it will be said to them: 'Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions.'"

None of the authors of the six books narrated it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Ahmad ibn Sinan, from 'Affan, with it. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Hammad ibn Salamah. [Al-Musnad (3/152) and Tafsir al-Tabari (18/141).]

Al-'Awfi said, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿Do not call out today for one destruction, but call out for many destructions﴾, that is: do not call out today for one woe, but call out for many woes.

Al-Dahhak said: al-thubur is destruction.

The most apparent view is that thubur combines destruction, woe, loss and ruin, as Musa said to Pharaoh: ﴿And indeed, I think you, O Pharaoh, are doomed (mathbur)﴾ [Al-Isra': 102], meaning: destroyed. And 'Abd Allah ibn al-Zib'ara said:

When I protect the devil in the paths of error,
and whoever inclines to his inclination is doomed (mathbur).

[The verse is in Ibn Hisham's al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (2/419).]

Allah the Exalted informs of the obstinacy, stubbornness and denial of the truth by the disbelievers, without any proof or evidence from them. They only offered excuses by saying: ﴿What is this Messenger that he eats food﴾, meaning: just as we eat it and need it as we need it; ﴿and walks in the markets﴾, that is, goes back and forth in them seeking gain and trade; ﴿Why has an angel not been sent down to him so that he could be a warner with him?﴾ They say: Why was an angel not sent down to him from Allah, to be a witness for him to the truth of what he claims! This is like what Pharaoh said: ﴿Why have bracelets of gold not been bestowed on him, or why have the angels not come with him in procession?﴾ [Az-Zukhruf: 53]. Likewise these people said the same, their hearts being alike. Therefore He said: ﴿Or a treasure be thrown down to him﴾, that is, the knowledge of a treasure [being] from which he could spend; ﴿or he have a garden from which he eats﴾, that is, one that moves with him wherever he goes. All of this is easy and simple for Allah, but for Him there is wisdom in leaving it, and for Him is the conclusive proof. ﴿And the wrongdoers said: You follow only a man affected by sorcery.﴾

Allah says: ﴿Look how they coin comparisons for you﴾, that is, they bring forth what they hurl at you and lie about you with, from their saying "a sorcerer, one affected by sorcery, a madman, a liar, a poet." All of these are false statements; everyone who has even a little understanding and intellect knows their lying and fabrication in this. Therefore He said: ﴿so they have gone astray﴾, that is, from the path of guidance, ﴿and they cannot find a way﴾. This is because whoever departs from the truth is astray wherever he turns, for the truth is one and its method is unified, each part confirming the others.

Then Allah the Exalted said, informing His Prophet that if He willed, He would give him better than what they say in this world, and finer and superior: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾

Mujahid said: this means in this world. He said: The Quraysh call every house of stone a palace, whether it is large or small.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Habib ibn Abi Thabit, from Khaythama: It was said to the Prophet ﷺ: "If you wish, we will give you the treasures of the earth and its keys, which no prophet before you was given, and none after you will be given, and that will not diminish what you have with Allah?" He said: "Gather them for me in the Hereafter." So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed concerning that: ﴿Blessed is He who, if He wills, will give you better than that: gardens beneath which rivers flow, and He will give you palaces.﴾ [Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/140) through Sufyan, as a mursal report.]

* *

Allah the Exalted says: O Muhammad, is this [[In manuscript A: "Is this"]] which We have described of the state of those wretched people, who will be gathered on their faces to Hell, where it will confront them with a scowling face, with rage and a roaring sound, and they will be thrown into its narrow places, bound together, unable to move, unable to get help, and unable to be freed from what they are in, better, or the Garden of Eternity which Allah has promised to His righteous servants, which He has prepared for them, made as a reward for their obedience to Him in the world, and made their final abode?

﴿For them therein is whatever they wish﴾, that is: of pleasures, including food and drink, clothing and dwellings, mounts and scenery, and other things, of which no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and no human heart has conceived. ﴿And they will abide therein forever﴾, eternally, perpetually, everlastingly, without interruption, cessation, or end, and they will not seek any change from it. This is from the promise of Allah, which He has bestowed upon them out of His grace and kindness. Therefore He said: ﴿It is ever a promise binding on your Lord to be fulfilled﴾, that is, it must certainly happen and come to pass. This is as Abu Ja'far ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) related from some scholars of the Arabic language, that the meaning of His words ﴿a promise to be fulfilled﴾ is: a promise that is obligatory.

Ibn Juraij said, from 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿It is ever a promise binding on your Lord to be fulfilled﴾: He says, "Ask of Him what He has promised you, or what We have promised you, and We will fulfill it."

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said regarding His words ﴿It is ever a promise binding on your Lord to be fulfilled﴾: "The angels will ask this for them: ﴿Our Lord, and admit them to the Gardens of Eternity which You have promised them﴾ [Ghafir: 8]."

Abu Hazim said: "When the Day of Resurrection comes, the believers will say: 'Our Lord, we have acted for You in accordance with what You commanded us, so fulfill for us what You promised us.' This is His saying: ﴿a promise to be fulfilled﴾."

The context of this passage in this surah is a mention of the Fire, followed by a reminder of the state of the people of Paradise, just as the Exalted mentioned in Surah "As-Saffat" the state of the people of Paradise and what is in it of radiance and joy, then said: ﴿Is that better as a welcome or the tree of Zaqqum? Indeed, We have made it a trial for the wrongdoers. Indeed, it is a tree that emerges from the root of Hellfire. Its emerging fruit is like the heads of devils. Indeed, they will eat from it and fill their bellies with it. Then indeed for them upon it is a mixture of scalding water. Then indeed their return is to Hellfire. Indeed, they found their fathers astray, so they rush in their footsteps﴾ [As-Saffat: 62–70].

He, may He be exalted, says, informing about what will happen on the Day of Resurrection of the rebuke of the disbelievers for their worship of those they worshipped besides Allah, among them the angels and others: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them, and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾. Mujahid said: "Jesus, Ezra (Uzayr), and the angels."

﴿Then He will say, "Did you mislead these My servants, or did they stray from the way themselves?"﴾ That is: the Lord, blessed and exalted, will say to the worshipped ones [[Added from A.]]: "Did you call these people to worship you besides Me, or did they worship you of their own accord, without any call from you to them?" As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Yours. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them only what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them while I remained among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them..."﴾ [[In manuscripts F and A, the following is added: "except what You commanded me, that worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord, and I was a witness over them while I remained among them; then when You took me up..."]] to the end of the verse [Al-Ma'idah: 116–117]. Therefore He, the Exalted, said, informing of what the worshipped will answer on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿They will say, "Exalted are You! It was not befitting for us to take any protectors besides You."﴾

Most readers recited "nattakhidha" (نَتَّخِذَ) with a fatha on the "nun" in His words "nattakhidha min dunika min awliya'" (نَتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ). That means: it is not for all creatures to worship anyone besides You, neither us nor them. We did not call them to that; rather they did that of their own accord, without Your command or Your pleasure, and we are free of them and of their worship. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them all, then says to the angels, "Did these people used to worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them believed in them."﴾ [Saba': 40–41]. [[In manuscript H: "bihi" (به), and the text as given in A is correct.]]

Others recited: "ma kana yanbaghi lana an nuttakhadha min dunika min awliya'" (مَا كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نُتَّخَذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ), meaning: it is not befitting for anyone to worship us, for we are servants of You, needy of You. Its meaning is close to the first reading.

﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment, until they forgot the Reminder.﴾ That is: long life passed over them until they forgot the Remembrance, that is, they forgot what You sent down to them through the tongues of Your messengers, namely the call to worship You alone, with no partner.

﴿And they were a people doomed.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: that is, destroyed. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Malik, from al-Zuhri, said: that is, there is no good in them. Ibn al-Za'bara, when he embraced Islam, said:

"O Messenger of the King, indeed my tongue
Mends what I have torn, since I have become doomed,
When I was contending with Satan in the paths of error,
And whoever inclines to his inclination is perished."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they will deny you in what you say﴾, that is: those you worshipped will deny you in what you claimed about them, that they were your protectors, and that you took them as intercessors who would bring you near to Allah in closeness. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are heedless of their call? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5–6].

And His words: ﴿So you cannot avert [the punishment] nor obtain help﴾ [[In manuscript A: "fala" (فلا), which is an error.]] That is: they will not be able to avert the punishment from themselves, nor to help themselves. ﴿And whoever of you wrongs﴾ that is, associates partners with Allah, ﴿We will make him taste a great punishment.﴾

It was not befitting for us to take any protectors besides You."﴾

Most readers recited "nattakhidha" (نَتَّخِذَ) with a fatha on the "nun" in His words "nattakhidha min dunika min awliya'" (نَتَّخِذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ). That means: it is not for all creatures to worship anyone besides You, neither us nor them. We did not call them to that; rather they did that of their own accord, without Your command or Your pleasure, and we are free of them and of their worship. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And on the Day He gathers them all, then says to the angels, "Did these people used to worship you?" They will say, "Exalted are You! You are our Protector, not them. Rather, they used to worship the jinn; most of them believed in them."﴾ [Saba': 40–41]. [[In manuscript H: "bihi" (به), and the text as given in A is correct.]]

Others recited: "ma kana yanbaghi lana an nuttakhadha min dunika min awliya'" (مَا كَانَ يَنْبَغِي لَنَا أَنْ نُتَّخَذَ مِنْ دُونِكَ مِنْ أَوْلِيَاءَ), meaning: it is not befitting for anyone to worship us, for we are servants of You, needy of You. Its meaning is close to the first reading.

﴿But You gave them and their fathers enjoyment, until they forgot the Reminder.﴾ That is: long life passed over them until they forgot the Remembrance, that is, they forgot what You sent down to them through the tongues of Your messengers, namely the call to worship You alone, with no partner.

﴿And they were a people doomed.﴾ Ibn Abbas said: that is, destroyed. Al-Hasan al-Basri and Malik, from al-Zuhri, said: that is, there is no good in them. Ibn al-Za'bara, when he embraced Islam, said:

"O Messenger of the King, indeed my tongue
Mends what I have torn, since I have become doomed,
When I was contending with Satan in the paths of error,
And whoever inclines to his inclination is perished."

Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿So they will deny you in what you say﴾, that is: those you worshipped will deny you in what you claimed about them, that they were your protectors, and that you took them as intercessors who would bring you near to Allah in closeness. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And who is more astray than one who calls upon other than Allah, one who will not respond to him until the Day of Resurrection, and they are heedless of their call? And when the people are gathered, they will be enemies to them and will deny their worship﴾ [Al-Ahqaf: 5–6].

And His words: ﴿So you cannot avert [the punishment] nor obtain help﴾ [[In manuscript A: "fala" (فلا), which is an error.]] That is: they will not be able to avert the punishment from themselves, nor to help themselves. ﴿And whoever of you wrongs﴾ that is, associates partners with Allah, ﴿We will make him taste a great punishment.﴾

He, may He be exalted, says, informing about what will happen on the Day of Resurrection of the rebuke of the disbelievers for their worship of those they worshipped besides Allah, among them the angels and others: ﴿And on the Day He will gather them, and what they worshipped besides Allah﴾. Mujahid said: "Jesus, Ezra (Uzayr), and the angels."

﴿Then He will say, "Did you mislead these My servants, or did they stray from the way themselves?"﴾ That is: the Lord, blessed and exalted, will say to the worshipped ones [[Added from A.]]: "Did you call these people to worship you besides Me, or did they worship you of their own accord, without any call from you to them?" As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And when Allah says, "O Jesus, son of Mary, did you say to the people, 'Take me and my mother as two gods besides Allah?'" He will say, "Exalted are You! It was not for me to say what I have no right to say. If I had said it, You would have known it. You know what is in my soul, and I do not know what is in Yours. Indeed, You are the Knower of the unseen. I said to them only what You commanded me: 'Worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord.' And I was a witness over them while I remained among them; but when You took me up, You were the Watcher over them..."﴾ [[In manuscripts F and A, the following is added: "except what You commanded me, that worship Allah, my Lord and your Lord, and I was a witness over them while I remained among them; then when You took me up..."]] to the end of the verse [Al-Ma'idah: 116–117]. Ibn Kathir said, explaining what Allah says about all the messengers He sent from among those before (Muhammad): They used to eat food and needed to nourish themselves with it, ﴿and walk in the markets﴾, meaning to earn a living and to trade. This is not contrary to their condition and rank, for Allah gave them good qualities, beautiful attributes, excellent words, complete deeds, astonishing extraordinary signs, and [overpowering] [[Addition from manuscript A.]] proofs, by which every person of sound intellect and upright insight is guided to the truth of what they brought from Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿And We sent before you only men to whom We revealed, from the people of the towns﴾ [Yusuf: 109] and ﴿We did not make them bodies that do not eat food, nor were they immortal﴾ [al-Anbiya: 8].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient?﴾, meaning: We tested some of you by means of others, and We tried some of you by others, so that We may know who obeys among those who disobey. Therefore He said: ﴿Will you be patient? And your Lord is ever Seeing﴾, meaning: He knows who deserves to be revealed to, as He said: ﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ [al-An'am: 124], and who deserves that Allah guide him to what He sent them with, and who does not deserve that.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, concerning His saying: ﴿And We have made some of you a trial for others. Will you be patient?﴾: Allah says: "If I had willed, I would have made the world subservient to My messengers so that they would not be opposed, and I would have done so. But I wanted to test the servants by means of them, and to test them [[In manuscript A: "and test you"]] by them."

In Sahih Muslim, from Iyad ibn Himar, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "Allah says: Indeed I will test you, and I will test through you." In the Musnad, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ: "If I wished, Allah would have made mountains of gold and silver flow with me." It is also established in the Sahih that he (peace and blessings be upon him) was given the choice between being a prophet-king or a servant-messenger, and he chose to be a servant-messenger.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verses 21–24 (part 1 of 2):

Allah the Exalted says, reporting the obstinacy of the disbelievers in their disbelief and their stubbornness in their words: ﴿Why have the angels not been sent down to us?﴾ [[In A: "عليه" (upon him), which is an error.]] That is, with the message, just as it was sent down upon the prophets. Allah the Exalted reported about them in another verse: ﴿They say, "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah."﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. It is also possible that their intention here was: ﴿Why have the angels not been sent down to us?﴾ so that we might see them with our own eyes, and they would tell us that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, like their saying: ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group.﴾ [al-Isra': 92]. Its interpretation has already been given in the surah of "Subhan" (al-Isra'). For this reason He said: ﴿Or let us see our Lord.﴾ For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and have committed great transgression.﴾ Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered before them all things, they would not have believed unless Allah willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ [al-An'am: 111].

* *

His saying: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals, and they will say, "A barrier forbidden."﴾ means: they will not see the angels on a day that is good for them; rather, on the day they see the angels, there will be no good news for them that day. This applies to the time of death, when the angels give the disbelievers tidings of the Fire and the wrath of the Compeller. The angels say to the disbeliever when his soul departs: "Come out, O wretched soul, in a wretched body. Come out to scorching wind and boiling water and a shade of black smoke." But it refuses to come out and scatters through the body, so they strike it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you could see when the angels take the lives of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs.﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. And He said: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming agonies of death and the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and for being arrogant toward His verses."﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. That is, by striking. For this reason He said in this noble verse: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals.﴾ This is in contrast to the condition of the believers at the time of their death, for they are given good news of good things and the attainment of joys. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you request, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Fussilat: 30–31].

It is reported in the authentic hadith from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib that the angels say to the soul of the believer: "Come out, O good soul, in a good body, which you used to inhabit. Come out to comfort and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry." [[The hadith has already been mentioned in the surah of "Ibrahim" (A: "المطمئنة" – "the tranquil")]] The hadith was already mentioned in the surah of "Ibrahim" [[At verse 27.]] at His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah sends astray the wrongdoers; and Allah does what He wills.﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others.

There is no contradiction between this and what preceded, for the angels on these two days, the day of death and the day of return, appear to the believers and to the disbelievers. They give the believers good news of mercy and pleasure, and they inform the disbelievers of loss and ruin. So there will be no good news that Day for the criminals.

﴿And they will say, "A barrier forbidden."﴾ That is: the angels will say to the disbelievers: "Forbidden and prohibited for you is salvation today."

The root meaning of "al-hijr" is prevention. From it one says: the judge placed a restriction (hajara) upon so-and-so when he prevented him from disposing of his property, whether due to foolishness, bankruptcy, minority, or the like. From it the "Hijr" beside the Sacred House (the Ka'bah) is named, because it prevents people from circumambulating within it; the circumambulation is performed from behind it. From it the intellect is called "hijr" [[In A: "حجرا"]], because it prevents its possessor from engaging in what is not fitting.

The point is that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and they will say﴾ refers to the angels. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Khusayf, and others. Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] chose it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/2).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Musa – meaning Ibn Qays – narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, regarding ﴿and they will say, "A barrier forbidden"﴾: He said: "Forbidden, prohibited, that they be given the good news that the God-fearing are given."

Ibn Jarir has related from Ibn Juraij that he said: That is from the speech of the polytheists: ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾ – that is, they seek refuge from the angels – for the Arabs, when a calamity or hardship befell one of them, would say: "A barrier forbidden."

Although this view has a basis and a reasoning behind it, it is distant in relation to the context of the verse, especially since the majority have explicitly stated otherwise. However, Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid that he said regarding His saying ﴿a barrier forbidden﴾: that is, "a refuge, a protection." So it is possible that he meant what Ibn Juraij mentioned. But in the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: ﴿a barrier forbidden﴾ [that is] [[Addition from A.]] "a refuge, a protection," said by the angels. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ This is on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah calls the servants to account for what they did of good and evil. He informs that nothing of the deeds that these polytheists thought would save them will be realized for them, because those deeds lacked the legislated condition: either sincerity in them, or conformity to the law of Allah. Every deed that is not sincere and in accordance with the approved Shari'ah is void. The deeds of the disbelievers do not lack one of these two conditions, and they may lack both together, and thus they are further from acceptance. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾

Mujahid and al-Thawri said: ﴿And We will turn﴾ means: We will intend.

Al-Suddi said: "Qadimna" means: We intended. Some of them say: We came upon it.

* *

His saying: ﴿and make them scattered dust﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿made them scattered dust﴾, that he said: "It is the ray of the sun when it enters through the window (kuwwa)." The same has been reported through other channels from 'Ali. Similar has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and others. Likewise al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It is the ray in the window of one of them [[In A and F: "أحدكم" – "one of you"]], and if he tried to grasp it he would not be able to."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿scattered dust﴾: He said: "It is spilled water."

Abu al-Ahwas narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali: ﴿scattered dust﴾: He said: "The dust is the dust raised by animals [[In F and A: "وهج" – "heat"]]." Similar has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas as well, and from al-Dahhak, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said it.

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿scattered dust﴾: "Have you not seen the dried-up tree when the wind scatters it? That is the leaves."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Asim ibn Hakim informed me, from Abu Sari' al-Ta'i, from Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd [[In A: "عبيد بن يعلى"]], who said: "Indeed, the dust is ash."

The sum of these sayings is an alert to the meaning of the verse: they performed deeds they believed to be something, but when these were presented to the Sovereign, the Wise, the Just, who does not oppress or wrong anyone, they were found to be nothing at all. They are likened in this to a trivial, worthless, scattered thing, from which its owner can obtain nothing whatsoever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ash which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and injury like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock with a layer of dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing.﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. The explanation of this has already preceded, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

His saying: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise – they are the attainers.﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. This is because the people of Paradise go to the high ranks and the secure chambers; they are in a secure station, of fine appearance and good dwelling, ﴿abiding therein; excellent it is as a place of settling and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 76]. The people of the Fire go to the lowest levels and successive regrets and various kinds of punishment and penalties, ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settling and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 66], that is: an evil dwelling in appearance and an evil resting place as a residence. For this reason He said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾ That is, because of the deeds they did that were accepted, they attained what they attained and reached what they reached. This is in contrast to the people of the Fire, for they have no single deed that would bring them entry into Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. Thus, by the condition of the happy ones, He alerted to the condition of the wretched, and that there is no good at all with them. He said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is only a forenoon, and the friends of Allah will rest on couches with the wide-eyed maidens, and the enemies of Allah will rest with the devils, bound together."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Allah will finish the reckoning at midday, and the people of Paradise will rest in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾

Ikrimah said: "I truly know the hour in which the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire. It is the hour in the world at the height of the greatest forenoon (al-Duha), when people return to their families for the midday rest (al-qaylulah). The people of the Fire are taken to the Fire, while the people of Paradise are taken to Paradise, and their midday rest is in Paradise. They are fed the liver of a fish (kabida hut), and it satisfies them all. This is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾."

Sufyan, from Maysarah, from al-Minhal, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "The day does not reach its midpoint until these and those have taken their midday rest." Then he recited: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, and he recited ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 68].

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, that he said: "They said: [this refers to] the chambers of the Garden. Their reckoning was that they were presented before their Lord in a single presentation, and that is the easy reckoning, like His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7-9]."

Qatadah said, regarding His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, that it means: a dwelling and a place of residence. Qatadah said: Safwan ibn Muhriz narrated that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection a man will be brought, one of whom was a king in the world, of the red and white (complexion), and he will be reckoned, and then he is found to be a slave who did no good, so he is ordered to the Fire. And the other was a man of a cloak in the world, and he will be reckoned and will say: 'O Lord, You gave me nothing that You would reckon me for.' He says: 'My servant has spoken truly, so release him.' He is ordered to Paradise. Then the two are left as Allah wills. Then the companion of the Fire is called, and he is like a black charcoal ember, and it is said to him: 'How did you find it?' He says: 'The worst resting place.' It is said to him: 'Return.' Then the companion of Paradise is called, and he is like the moon on the night of the full moon, and it is said to him: 'How did you find it?' He says: 'My Lord, the best resting place.' It is said to him: 'Return.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of these.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, that Ibn Wahb informed us, that Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, that Sa'id al-Saddaf narrated to him that it reached him: that on the Day of Resurrection the day will be shortened for the believer until it is as (long as) what lies between the afternoon prayer and the sunset, and that they will take their midday rest in the gardens of Paradise until people are finished (with the reckoning). And that is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/5).]
