Allah the Exalted reported about them in another verse: ﴿They say, "We will not believe until we are given what was given to the messengers of Allah."﴾ [al-An'am: 124]. It is also possible that their intention here was: ﴿Why have the angels not been sent down to us?﴾ so that we might see them with our own eyes, and they would tell us that Muhammad is the Messenger of Allah, like their saying: ﴿Or you bring Allah and the angels before us as a group.﴾ [al-Isra': 92]. Its interpretation has already been given in the surah of "Subhan" (al-Isra'). For this reason He said: ﴿Or let us see our Lord.﴾ For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They have certainly become arrogant within themselves and have committed great transgression.﴾ Allah the Exalted also said: ﴿And even if We had sent down to them the angels and the dead had spoken to them and We had gathered before them all things, they would not have believed unless Allah willed; but most of them are ignorant.﴾ [al-An'am: 111].

* *

His saying: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals, and they will say, "A barrier forbidden."﴾ means: they will not see the angels on a day that is good for them; rather, on the day they see the angels, there will be no good news for them that day. This applies to the time of death, when the angels give the disbelievers tidings of the Fire and the wrath of the Compeller. The angels say to the disbeliever when his soul departs: "Come out, O wretched soul, in a wretched body. Come out to scorching wind and boiling water and a shade of black smoke." But it refuses to come out and scatters through the body, so they strike it, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿If you could see when the angels take the lives of those who disbelieve, striking their faces and their backs.﴾ [al-Anfal: 50]. And He said: ﴿If you could see when the wrongdoers are in the overwhelming agonies of death and the angels extend their hands, [saying], "Release your souls. Today you will be recompensed with the punishment of humiliation for what you used to say about Allah other than the truth and for being arrogant toward His verses."﴾ [al-An'am: 93]. That is, by striking. For this reason He said in this noble verse: ﴿On the Day they see the angels, there will be no good news that Day for the criminals.﴾ This is in contrast to the condition of the believers at the time of their death, for they are given good news of good things and the attainment of joys. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who say, "Our Lord is Allah," and then remain steadfast, the angels will descend upon them, [saying], "Do not fear and do not grieve, but receive good news of Paradise, which you were promised. We are your allies in the life of this world and in the Hereafter. And for you therein is what your souls desire, and for you therein is what you request, as a welcome from the Forgiving, the Merciful."﴾ [Fussilat: 30–31].

It is reported in the authentic hadith from al-Bara' ibn 'Azib that the angels say to the soul of the believer: "Come out, O good soul, in a good body, which you used to inhabit. Come out to comfort and fragrance and a Lord who is not angry." [[The hadith has already been mentioned in the surah of "Ibrahim" (A: "المطمئنة" – "the tranquil")]] The hadith was already mentioned in the surah of "Ibrahim" [[At verse 27.]] at His saying: ﴿Allah keeps firm those who believe with the firm word in worldly life and in the Hereafter, and Allah sends astray the wrongdoers; and Allah does what He wills.﴾ [Ibrahim: 27].

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾ is the Day of Resurrection. This was said by Mujahid, al-Dahhak, and others.

There is no contradiction between this and what preceded, for the angels on these two days, the day of death and the day of return, appear to the believers and to the disbelievers. They give the believers good news of mercy and pleasure, and they inform the disbelievers of loss and ruin. So there will be no good news that Day for the criminals.

﴿And they will say, "A barrier forbidden."﴾ That is: the angels will say to the disbelievers: "Forbidden and prohibited for you is salvation today."

The root meaning of "al-hijr" is prevention. From it one says: the judge placed a restriction (hajara) upon so-and-so when he prevented him from disposing of his property, whether due to foolishness, bankruptcy, minority, or the like. From it the "Hijr" beside the Sacred House (the Ka'bah) is named, because it prevents people from circumambulating within it; the circumambulation is performed from behind it. From it the intellect is called "hijr" [[In A: "حجرا"]], because it prevents its possessor from engaging in what is not fitting.

The point is that the pronoun in His saying ﴿and they will say﴾ refers to the angels. This is the view of Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan, Qatadah, 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, 'Ata' al-Khurasani, Khusayf, and others. Ibn Jarir [al-Tabari] chose it. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (19/2).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Nu'aym narrated to us, Musa – meaning Ibn Qays – narrated to us, from 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, regarding ﴿and they will say, "A barrier forbidden"﴾: He said: "Forbidden, prohibited, that they be given the good news that the God-fearing are given."

Ibn Jarir has related from Ibn Juraij that he said: That is from the speech of the polytheists: ﴿On the Day they see the angels﴾ – that is, they seek refuge from the angels – for the Arabs, when a calamity or hardship befell one of them, would say: "A barrier forbidden."

Although this view has a basis and a reasoning behind it, it is distant in relation to the context of the verse, especially since the majority have explicitly stated otherwise. However, Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid that he said regarding His saying ﴿a barrier forbidden﴾: that is, "a refuge, a protection." So it is possible that he meant what Ibn Juraij mentioned. But in the narration of Ibn Abi Hatim, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, he said: ﴿a barrier forbidden﴾ [that is] [[Addition from A.]] "a refuge, a protection," said by the angels. And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying the Exalted: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾ This is on the Day of Resurrection, when Allah calls the servants to account for what they did of good and evil. He informs that nothing of the deeds that these polytheists thought would save them will be realized for them, because those deeds lacked the legislated condition: either sincerity in them, or conformity to the law of Allah. Every deed that is not sincere and in accordance with the approved Shari'ah is void. The deeds of the disbelievers do not lack one of these two conditions, and they may lack both together, and thus they are further from acceptance. For this reason Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust.﴾

Mujahid and al-Thawri said: ﴿And We will turn﴾ means: We will intend.

Al-Suddi said: "Qadimna" means: We intended. Some of them say: We came upon it.

* *

His saying: ﴿and make them scattered dust﴾. Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, regarding His saying: ﴿made them scattered dust﴾, that he said: "It is the ray of the sun when it enters through the window (kuwwa)." The same has been reported through other channels from 'Ali. Similar has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Suddi, al-Dahhak, and others. Likewise al-Hasan al-Basri said: "It is the ray in the window of one of them [[In A and F: "أحدكم" – "one of you"]], and if he tried to grasp it he would not be able to."

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿scattered dust﴾: He said: "It is spilled water."

Abu al-Ahwas narrated from Abu Ishaq, from al-Harith, from 'Ali: ﴿scattered dust﴾: He said: "The dust is the dust raised by animals [[In F and A: "وهج" – "heat"]]." Similar has been reported from Ibn 'Abbas as well, and from al-Dahhak, and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said it.

Qatadah said regarding His saying: ﴿scattered dust﴾: "Have you not seen the dried-up tree when the wind scatters it? That is the leaves."

'Abd Allah ibn Wahb said: Asim ibn Hakim informed me, from Abu Sari' al-Ta'i, from Ya'la ibn 'Ubayd [[In A: "عبيد بن يعلى"]], who said: "Indeed, the dust is ash."

The sum of these sayings is an alert to the meaning of the verse: they performed deeds they believed to be something, but when these were presented to the Sovereign, the Wise, the Just, who does not oppress or wrong anyone, they were found to be nothing at all. They are likened in this to a trivial, worthless, scattered thing, from which its owner can obtain nothing whatsoever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The example of those who disbelieve in their Lord is that their deeds are like ash which the wind blows forcefully on a stormy day; they have no power over anything of what they have earned. That is the far-reaching error.﴾ [Ibrahim: 18]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿O you who believe, do not invalidate your charities with reminders and injury like one who spends his wealth to be seen by people and does not believe in Allah and the Last Day. His example is like a smooth rock with a layer of dust on it; a heavy rain strikes it and leaves it bare. They have no power over anything of what they have earned.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 264]. And He the Exalted said: ﴿And those who disbelieve, their deeds are like a mirage in a level desert which the thirsty one thinks is water, until, when he comes to it, he finds it to be nothing.﴾ [al-Nur: 39]. The explanation of this has already preceded, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

* *

His saying: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾ That is, on the Day of Resurrection: ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise – they are the attainers.﴾ [al-Hashr: 20]. This is because the people of Paradise go to the high ranks and the secure chambers; they are in a secure station, of fine appearance and good dwelling, ﴿abiding therein; excellent it is as a place of settling and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 76]. The people of the Fire go to the lowest levels and successive regrets and various kinds of punishment and penalties, ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settling and residence.﴾ [al-Furqan: 66], that is: an evil dwelling in appearance and an evil resting place as a residence. For this reason He said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾ That is, because of the deeds they did that were accepted, they attained what they attained and reached what they reached. This is in contrast to the people of the Fire, for they have no single deed that would bring them entry into Paradise and deliverance from the Fire. Thus, by the condition of the happy ones, He alerted to the condition of the wretched, and that there is no good at all with them. He said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn 'Abbas: "It is only a forenoon, and the friends of Allah will rest on couches with the wide-eyed maidens, and the enemies of Allah will rest with the devils, bound together."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "Allah will finish the reckoning at midday, and the people of Paradise will rest in Paradise and the people of the Fire in the Fire." Allah the Exalted said: ﴿The companions of Paradise, that Day, will be better in residence and finer in resting place.﴾

Ikrimah said: "I truly know the hour in which the people of Paradise enter Paradise and the people of the Fire enter the Fire. It is the hour in the world at the height of the greatest forenoon (al-Duha), when people return to their families for the midday rest (al-qaylulah). The people of the Fire are taken to the Fire, while the people of Paradise are taken to Paradise, and their midday rest is in Paradise. They are fed the liver of a fish (kabida hut), and it satisfies them all. This is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾."

Sufyan, from Maysarah, from al-Minhal, from Abu Ubaydah, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, that he said: "The day does not reach its midpoint until these and those have taken their midday rest." Then he recited: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, and he recited ﴿Then indeed their return is to the Blazing Fire﴾ [al-Saffat: 68].

Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas, regarding His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, that he said: "They said: [this refers to] the chambers of the Garden. Their reckoning was that they were presented before their Lord in a single presentation, and that is the easy reckoning, like His saying: ﴿As for him who is given his record in his right hand, he will be called to an easy reckoning, and he will return to his family rejoicing﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 7-9]."

Qatadah said, regarding His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾, that it means: a dwelling and a place of residence. Qatadah said: Safwan ibn Muhriz narrated that he said: "On the Day of Resurrection a man will be brought, one of whom was a king in the world, of the red and white (complexion), and he will be reckoned, and then he is found to be a slave who did no good, so he is ordered to the Fire. And the other was a man of a cloak in the world, and he will be reckoned and will say: 'O Lord, You gave me nothing that You would reckon me for.' He says: 'My servant has spoken truly, so release him.' He is ordered to Paradise. Then the two are left as Allah wills. Then the companion of the Fire is called, and he is like a black charcoal ember, and it is said to him: 'How did you find it?' He says: 'The worst resting place.' It is said to him: 'Return.' Then the companion of Paradise is called, and he is like the moon on the night of the full moon, and it is said to him: 'How did you find it?' He says: 'My Lord, the best resting place.' It is said to him: 'Return.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated all of these.

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to me, that Ibn Wahb informed us, that Amr ibn al-Harith informed us, that Sa'id al-Saddaf narrated to him that it reached him: that on the Day of Resurrection the day will be shortened for the believer until it is as (long as) what lies between the afternoon prayer and the sunset, and that they will take their midday rest in the gardens of Paradise until people are finished (with the reckoning). And that is His saying: ﴿The companions of the Garden on that Day will have a better abode and a finer resting place﴾. [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/5).]

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 25, verses 25–29:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the great events that will occur on it. Among them is the splitting and rending of the sky and its being torn open with the clouds, and these are canopies of the great Light that dazzles the eyes. On that day the angels of the heavens will descend and surround the creatures in the place of gathering. Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, will come to judge between them.

Mujahid said: This is as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels, and the matter be decided? And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Mu'ammal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited this verse: ﴿And the day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection onto one level plain: the jinn, the humans, the animals, the beasts of prey, the birds, and all creatures. Then the lowest heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the jinn and the humans and all creatures. They will surround the jinn, the humans, and all creatures. Then the second heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the people of the lowest heaven, and than the jinn and humans and all creatures, [so they surround the angels who descended before them, and the jinn and humans and all creatures]. [This addition is from manuscripts (f) and (a) and al-Durr al-Manthur 5/68.] Then the third heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the inhabitants of the second heaven and the lowest heaven and all creatures. They will surround the angels who descended before them, and the jinn and humans and all creatures. Then likewise for every heaven, until the seventh heaven is split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than those who descended before them from the inhabitants of the heavens, and than the jinn and humans and all creatures. They will surround the angels who descended before them from the inhabitants of the heavens, and the jinn and humans and all creatures. Our Lord, mighty and majestic, will descend in canopies of clouds, and around Him will be the Karubiyun (the angels nearest the Throne), who are more numerous than the inhabitants of the seven heavens and the humans and jinn and all creatures. They have horns like the knots of spears, and they are beneath the Throne. They have a resounding voice of glorification, declaration of Allah's oneness (tahlil), and sanctification of Allah, mighty and majestic. The distance between the sole of one of them and his ankle is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his ankle and his knee is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his knee and his hip is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his hip and his collarbone is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his collarbone and the place of the earring is a five-hundred-year journey; and what is above that is a five-hundred-year journey. And Jahannam is at his side. [This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with this wording.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When this heaven is split open, more angels will descend from it than jinn and humans. This is the Day of Meeting (yawm al-talaq), the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet. The people of the earth will say: "Has our Lord come?" and they will say: "He has not come, but He is coming." Then the second heaven will be split open, then heaven after heaven in proportion to that multiplication, up to the seventh heaven. Then more angels will descend from it than all those who descended from the heavens, and than the jinn and humans. He said: The Karubiyun angels will descend, then our Lord will come in the carrying of the eight bearers of the Throne. The distance between the ankle of each king and his knee is a seventy-year journey, and between his thigh and his shoulder is a seventy-year journey. He said: Each one of them does not look at the face of his companion, and each one of them places his head between his breasts saying: "Glory be to the King, the Holy." Above their heads is something spread out like a qaba' (a cloak), and the Throne is above that.

Then the narration stops. Its transmission depends on 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, in whom there is weakness, and its contexts are generally extremely strange. Something similar to this has been reported in the well-known hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur), which was mentioned in the commentary on verse 73 of Surah al-An'am. And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Then on that Day the Event will occur, and the sky will be split, for it will be frail that Day, and the angels will be upon its edges. And above them that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15–17] Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The bearers of the Throne are eight. Four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge." And four say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your pardon after Your power." Ibn Jarir narrated it from him.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the people of the earth look at the Throne descending upon them from above them, their eyes will be fixed on it, their hearts will tremble within their bodies, and their hearts will fly from their places in their chests up to their throats.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Jalil, from Abu Hazim, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: Allah, when He descends, will have between Himself and His creation seventy thousand veils, some of which are light and some darkness. The water will then make a sound in that darkness, a sound by which the hearts will be torn from their places.

This is a statement attributed to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr as his own words, and perhaps it comes from the two "burden-bearing" camels (al-zamilatan, a term Ibn Kathir uses for transmitters of Isra'iliyyat, i.e., Israelite narratives), and Allah knows best.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿The sovereignty on that Day will be entirely for the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.﴾ is as Allah said: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. In the Sahih: "Indeed Allah will fold the heavens with His right hand, and take the earths with His other hand, then say: I am the King. I am the Judge. Where are the kings of the earth? Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?" [Sahih Muslim no. 2788, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. The words "I am the Judge" are not in it.]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾ means: severe and hard, because it is a day of justice and decisive judgment, as Allah said: ﴿[When the trumpet is blown]﴾ [Added from manuscripts (f) and (a)] ﴿So that will be, that Day, a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 8–10] This is the condition of the disbelievers on this day. As for the believers, Allah said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them: "This is your Day which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, [regarding] ﴿a day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, how long this day will be!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it will be made so light for the believer that it will be lighter for him than an obligatory prayer he prayed in the world." [Musnad 3/75. In its chain is Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, who is weak.]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And the day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying: "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger."﴾ Allah informs us of the regret of the wrongdoer who departed from the path of the Messenger and what he brought from Allah of the clear truth, about which there is no doubt, and took another path other than the way of the Messenger. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will regret where regret will not benefit him, and he will bite his hands in grief and sorrow.

Whether the cause of its revelation concerned 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt or others among the wretched, it is general to every wrongdoer, as Allah said: ﴿The Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger." And they will say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they misled us from the way." Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66–68] So every wrongdoer will regret on the Day of Resurrection to the utmost extent of regret, biting his hands, saying: ﴿Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger. Oh, woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend.﴾ That is, the one who turned him away from guidance and diverted him to the path of misguidance [from the callers to misguidance (added from manuscripts (f) and (a))]. In this, it makes no difference whether it is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, or his brother Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or others.

﴿He had already led me away from the Reminder [meaning the Qur'an (added from manuscripts (f) and (a))] after it had come to me.﴾ That is, after it had reached me. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Satan is ever, for man, a deserter (khadhul).﴾ That is, he forsakes him from the truth, turns him away from it, employs him in falsehood, and calls him to it.

Ibn Kathir, *Tafsir al-Qur'an al-'Azim*, on Surah 25, verses 25–29:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us about the terror of the Day of Resurrection and the great events that will occur on it. Among them is the splitting and rending of the sky and its being torn open with the clouds, and these are canopies of the great Light that dazzles the eyes. On that day the angels of the heavens will descend and surround the creatures in the place of gathering. Then the Lord, blessed and exalted, will come to judge between them.

Mujahid said: This is as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Do they await only that Allah should come to them in canopies of clouds, and the angels, and the matter be decided? And to Allah all matters are returned.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 210]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn al-Harith narrated to us, Mu'ammal narrated to us, Hammad ibn Salamah narrated to us, from 'Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he recited this verse: ﴿And the day the sky will be split open with clouds, and the angels will be sent down, descending.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah will gather the creation on the Day of Resurrection onto one level plain: the jinn, the humans, the animals, the beasts of prey, the birds, and all creatures. Then the lowest heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the jinn and the humans and all creatures. They will surround the jinn, the humans, and all creatures. Then the second heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the people of the lowest heaven, and than the jinn and humans and all creatures, [so they surround the angels who descended before them, and the jinn and humans and all creatures]. [This addition is from manuscripts (f) and (a) and al-Durr al-Manthur 5/68.] Then the third heaven will be split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than the inhabitants of the second heaven and the lowest heaven and all creatures. They will surround the angels who descended before them, and the jinn and humans and all creatures. Then likewise for every heaven, until the seventh heaven is split open, and its inhabitants will descend, and they are more numerous than those who descended before them from the inhabitants of the heavens, and than the jinn and humans and all creatures. They will surround the angels who descended before them from the inhabitants of the heavens, and the jinn and humans and all creatures. Our Lord, mighty and majestic, will descend in canopies of clouds, and around Him will be the Karubiyun (the angels nearest the Throne), who are more numerous than the inhabitants of the seven heavens and the humans and jinn and all creatures. They have horns like the knots of spears, and they are beneath the Throne. They have a resounding voice of glorification, declaration of Allah's oneness (tahlil), and sanctification of Allah, mighty and majestic. The distance between the sole of one of them and his ankle is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his ankle and his knee is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his knee and his hip is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his hip and his collarbone is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his collarbone and the place of the earring is a five-hundred-year journey; and what is above that is a five-hundred-year journey. And Jahannam is at his side. [This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with this wording.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When this heaven is split open, more angels will descend from it than jinn and humans. This is the Day of Meeting (yawm al-talaq), the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet. The people of the earth will say: "Has our Lord come?" and they will say: "He has not come, but He is coming." They have horns like the knots of spears, and they are beneath the Throne. They have a resounding voice of glorification, declaration of Allah's oneness (tahlil), and sanctification of Allah, mighty and majestic. The distance between the sole of one of them and his ankle is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his ankle and his knee is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his knee and his hip is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his hip and his collarbone is a five-hundred-year journey; the distance between his collarbone and the place of the earring is a five-hundred-year journey; and what is above that is a five-hundred-year journey. And Jahannam is at his side. [This is how Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it with this wording.]

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, al-Hajjaj narrated to me, from Mubarak ibn Fadalah, from 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, that he heard Ibn 'Abbas say: When this heaven is split open, more angels will descend from it than jinn and humans. This is the Day of Meeting (yawm al-talaq), the day when the people of the heavens and the people of the earth meet. The people of the earth will say: "Has our Lord come?" and they will say: "He has not come, but He is coming." Then the second heaven will be split open, then heaven after heaven in proportion to that multiplication, up to the seventh heaven. Then more angels will descend from it than all those who descended from the heavens, and than the jinn and humans. He said: The Karubiyun angels will descend, then our Lord will come in the carrying of the eight bearers of the Throne. The distance between the ankle of each king and his knee is a seventy-year journey, and between his thigh and his shoulder is a seventy-year journey. He said: Each one of them does not look at the face of his companion, and each one of them places his head between his breasts saying: "Glory be to the King, the Holy." Above their heads is something spread out like a qaba' (a cloak), and the Throne is above that.

Then the narration stops. Its transmission depends on 'Ali ibn Zayd ibn Jud'an, in whom there is weakness, and its contexts are generally extremely strange. Something similar to this has been reported in the well-known hadith of the Trumpet (al-Sur), which was mentioned in the commentary on verse 73 of Surah al-An'am. And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, also said: ﴿Then on that Day the Event will occur, and the sky will be split, for it will be frail that Day, and the angels will be upon its edges. And above them that Day eight will bear the Throne of your Lord.﴾ [al-Haqqah: 15–17] Shahr ibn Hawshab said: The bearers of the Throne are eight. Four of them say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your forbearance after Your knowledge." And four say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, and praise be to You. To You be praise for Your pardon after Your power." Ibn Jarir narrated it from him.

Abu Bakr ibn 'Abd Allah said: When the people of the earth look at the Throne descending upon them from above them, their eyes will be fixed on it, their hearts will tremble within their bodies, and their hearts will fly from their places in their chests up to their throats.

Ibn Jarir said: al-Qasim narrated to us, al-Husayn narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from 'Abd al-Jalil, from Abu Hazim, from 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr, who said: Allah, when He descends, will have between Himself and His creation seventy thousand veils, some of which are light and some darkness. The water will then make a sound in that darkness, a sound by which the hearts will be torn from their places.

This is a statement attributed to 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr as his own words, and perhaps it comes from the two "burden-bearing" camels (al-zamilatan, a term Ibn Kathir uses for transmitters of Isra'iliyyat, i.e., Israelite narratives), and Allah knows best.

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿The sovereignty on that Day will be entirely for the Most Merciful, and it will be a difficult Day for the disbelievers.﴾ is as Allah said: ﴿Whose is the dominion today? It is for Allah, the One, the Subduer.﴾ [Ghafir: 16]. In the Sahih: "Indeed Allah will fold the heavens with His right hand, and take the earths with His other hand, then say: I am the King. I am the Judge. Where are the kings of the earth? Where are the tyrants? Where are the arrogant?" [Sahih Muslim no. 2788, from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him. The words "I am the Judge" are not in it.]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿and it will be a difficult day for the disbelievers﴾ means: severe and hard, because it is a day of justice and decisive judgment, as Allah said: ﴿[When the trumpet is blown]﴾ [Added from manuscripts (f) and (a)] ﴿So that will be, that Day, a difficult day, not easy for the disbelievers.﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 8–10] This is the condition of the disbelievers on this day. As for the believers, Allah said: ﴿The greatest terror will not grieve them, and the angels will receive them: "This is your Day which you were promised."﴾ [al-Anbiya': 103]

Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to us, Darraj narrated to us, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of Allah, [regarding] ﴿a day whose measure is fifty thousand years﴾, how long this day will be!" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, it will be made so light for the believer that it will be lighter for him than an obligatory prayer he prayed in the world." [Musnad 3/75. In its chain is Darraj from Abu al-Haytham, who is weak.]

* *

Allah's saying: ﴿And the day the wrongdoer will bite on his hands, saying: "Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger."﴾ Allah informs us of the regret of the wrongdoer who departed from the path of the Messenger and what he brought from Allah of the clear truth, about which there is no doubt, and took another path other than the way of the Messenger. So when the Day of Resurrection comes, he will regret where regret will not benefit him, and he will bite his hands in grief and sorrow.

Whether the cause of its revelation concerned 'Uqbah ibn Abi Mu'ayt or others among the wretched, it is general to every wrongdoer, as Allah said: ﴿The Day their faces will be turned over in the Fire, they will say: "Oh, would that we had obeyed Allah and obeyed the Messenger." And they will say: "Our Lord, indeed we obeyed our leaders and our elders, and they misled us from the way." Our Lord, give them double the punishment and curse them with a great curse.﴾ [al-Ahzab: 66–68] So every wrongdoer will regret on the Day of Resurrection to the utmost extent of regret, biting his hands, saying: ﴿Oh, would that I had taken a way with the Messenger. Oh, woe to me! Would that I had not taken so-and-so as a close friend.﴾ That is, the one who turned him away from guidance and diverted him to the path of misguidance [from the callers to misguidance (added from manuscripts (f) and (a))]. In this, it makes no difference whether it is Umayyah ibn Khalaf, or his brother Ubayy ibn Khalaf, or others.

﴿He had already led me away from the Reminder [meaning the Qur'an (added from manuscripts (f) and (a))] after it had come to me.﴾ That is, after it had reached me. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And Satan is ever, for man, a deserter (khadhul).﴾ That is, he forsakes him from the truth, turns him away from it, employs him in falsehood, and calls him to it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verses 30–31:

Allah, exalted is He, informs about His Messenger and Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him always until the Day of Judgement, that he said: ﴿O my Lord, my people have taken this Qur'an as something abandoned.﴾ This is because the polytheists would not give ear to the Qur'an, nor would they listen to it, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during its recitation that you may overcome [it]."﴾ [Fussilat: 26]. Whenever the Qur'an was recited to them, they would raise a great clamour and talk about other things, so that they would not hear it. This is among its abandonment (hijran). Also, neglecting its knowledge (ilm) and its memorisation (hifz) is among its abandonment; neglecting faith in it and affirming its truth is among its abandonment; neglecting its contemplation (tadabbur) and understanding (tafahhum) is among its abandonment; neglecting to act upon it, to carry out its commands and to avoid its prohibitions is among its abandonment; and turning away from it to something else, whether poetry, speech, singing, amusement, talk, or a way of life taken from others, is among its abandonment.

So we ask Allah, the Generous, the Bestower, the One Able to do what He wills, to free us from what displeases Him, and to employ us in what pleases Him: in memorising His Book and understanding it, and in acting upon its requirements during the hours of the night and the extremities of the day, in the manner that He loves and approves. Indeed, He is Generous, the Bestower.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals﴾, that is: just as there happened to you, O Muhammad, among your people, from those who abandoned the Qur'an, so it was among the earlier nations. For Allah appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals, who call people to their misguidance and disbelief, as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy: devils among mankind and jinn, inspiring to one another decorative speech as deception. And if your Lord had willed, they would not have done it, so leave them and what they invent. And let the hearts of those who do not believe in the Hereafter incline to it, and let them be pleased with it, and let them commit what they are committing.﴾ [Al-An'am: 112–113]. For this reason He said here: ﴿And sufficient is your Lord as guide and helper.﴾ That is: for whoever follows His Messenger, believes in His Book, affirms it and follows it, Allah is his guide and helper in this world and the Hereafter. He said ﴿as guide and helper﴾ specifically because the polytheists used to turn people away from following the Qur'an, so that no one would be guided by it, and so that their way would prevail over the way of the Qur'an. Therefore He said: ﴿And thus We have appointed for every prophet an enemy from among the criminals; and sufficient is your Lord as guide and helper.﴾

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said, regarding the great number of the disbelievers' objections, their obstinacy, and their speaking about matters that do not concern them, where they said: ﴿Why was the Qur'an not sent down to him all at once?﴾ That is: why was this Book that was revealed to him not sent down all at once, as the earlier scriptures were sent down before him, such as the Torah, the Injil (Gospel), the Zabur (Psalms), and other divine books?

Allah answered them concerning that: it was revealed in installments (munajjaman) over twenty-three years, according to events and occurrences, and according to the rulings needed, in order to make the hearts of the believers in it firm, as He said: ﴿And (it is) a Qur'an which We have separated (in revelation) that you might recite it to the people at intervals, and We have sent it down in stages.﴾ [al-Isra': 106]. For this reason He said: ﴿Thus (it was revealed) that We may strengthen thereby your heart, and We have spaced it distinctly.﴾ Qatadah said: "And We have explained it with clear explanation." 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: "And We have interpreted it with (fine) interpretation."

﴿And they do not come to you with an argument⦆ That is: with a proof or a doubt, ﴿but We bring you the truth and the best explanation.﴾ That is: they do not say any statement by which they oppose the truth, except that We answer them with what is the truth in reality, and is clearer, more manifest, and more eloquent than their statement.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr narrated from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿And they do not come to you with an argument﴾ means: with that by which they seek to find fault with the Qur'an and the Messenger, ﴿but We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾ means: except that Jibril descends from Allah with their answer.

Then in this there is great honour for the Messenger (ﷺ), since the revelation of the Qur'an came to him from Allah morning and evening, by night and by day, while travelling and while at home. Each time the angel came to him with the Qur'an, it was like the sending down of a Book, in addition to the earlier scriptures. This station is higher and more exalted, and greater in rank, than that of his brothers among the Prophets, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon them all. The Qur'an is therefore the most noble Book that Allah has sent down, and Muhammad (ﷺ) is the greatest Prophet Allah has sent. Allah has combined for the Qur'an both attributes together: it was sent down as a whole from the Preserved Tablet to the House of Honour (Bayt al-'Izzah) in the lowest heaven, and then it was sent down to the earth in installments according to events and occurrences.

Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i said: Ahmad ibn Sulayman informed us, Yazid ibn Harun narrated to us, Dawud informed us, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: The Qur'an was sent down all at once to the lowest heaven on the Night of Decree (Laylat al-Qadr), and then it was sent down afterward over twenty years. He said: ﴿And they do not come to you with an argument but We bring you the truth and the best explanation﴾, and His saying ﴿And (it is) a Qur'an which We have separated (in revelation) that you might recite it to the people at intervals, and We have sent it down in stages.﴾ [al-Isra': 106] [al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11372].

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, informing about the evil state of the disbelievers in their return on the Day of Resurrection and their gathering into Hell, in the worst conditions and most ugly attributes: ﴿Those who will be gathered on their faces to Hell — those are worse in position and further astray from the way.﴾ In the Sahih, from Anas: a man said, "O Messenger of Allah, how will the disbeliever be gathered on his face on the Day of Resurrection?" He said: "The One who made him walk on his feet is able to make him walk on his face on the Day of Resurrection." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4760, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2806]. Likewise said Mujahid, al-Hasan, Qatadah, and other than one of the exegetes. [And Allah knows best.]

Allah, exalted is He, says, warning those among the polytheists of his people who denied His Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, and who opposed him, and warning them of His punishment and painful torment, of what He brought down upon the earlier nations who denied their messengers. He begins by mentioning Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, and that He sent him and made his brother Harun (Aaron) a minister with him, meaning a prophet who would support, strengthen and assist him. Pharaoh and his soldiers denied them both, so ﴿Allah destroyed them utterly, and for the disbelievers there are similar [fates]﴾ [Muhammad: 10]. He likewise did to the people of Nuh (Noah) when they denied His messenger Nuh, peace be upon him. Whoever denies one messenger has denied all the messengers, since there is no distinction between one messenger and another. Even if it were supposed that Allah had sent to them every messenger, they would have denied each of them. Therefore He said: ﴿and the people of Nuh when they denied the messengers﴾, although only Nuh was sent to them. He remained among them a thousand years less fifty years, calling them to Allah and warning them of His vengeance, yet only a few believed with him. For this reason Allah drowned them all, and none of them remained, and on the face of the earth none of the children of Adam remained except the people of the ship alone.

﴿And We made them a sign for the people﴾, meaning a lesson by which they may take warning, as Allah says: ﴿Indeed, when the water overflowed, We carried you in the sailing ship, that We might make it for you a reminder, and that a retaining ear might retain it﴾ [al-Haqqah: 11-12]. That is, We preserved for you of ships what you ride upon in the depths of the seas, so that you might remember Allah's blessing upon you in saving you from drowning, and in making you descendants of those who believed in Him and affirmed His command.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and ʿAd and Thamud﴾, the account of both has already been discussed in more than one surah, including in Surat al-Aʿraf, sufficiently so as to dispense with repetition.

As for the People of the Rass (al-Rass, a well or pit), Ibn Jurayj reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: they were the people of a town from the towns of Thamud.

Ibn Jurayj also said: ʿIkrimah said, the People of the Rass were at Falaj, and they are the People of Ya-Sin. Qatadah said: Falaj is one of the towns of al-Yamamah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn ʿAmr ibn Abi ʿAsim [al-Nabil] narrated to us, al-Dahhak ibn Makhlad Abu ʿAsim narrated to us, Shabib ibn Bishr narrated to us, ʿIkrimah narrated to us from Ibn ʿAbbas, regarding His saying: ﴿and the People of the Rass﴾, he said: a well in Adharbayjan.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Bukayr, from ʿIkrimah: al-Rass is a well into which they cast their prophet, meaning they buried him therein.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb [al-Qurazi]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection is the black slave. As for His saying: ﴿and ʿAd and Thamud﴾, the account of both has already been discussed in more than one surah, including in Surat al-Aʿraf, sufficiently so as to dispense with repetition.

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Abu Bukayr, from ʿIkrimah: al-Rass is a well into which they cast their prophet, meaning they buried him therein.

Muhammad ibn Ishaq said, from Muhammad ibn Kaʿb [al-Qurazi]: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The first of mankind to enter Paradise on the Day of Resurrection is the black slave. Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verses 45–47:

From here, Exalted is He, He began to explain the proofs that point to His existence and His complete power to create different and opposing things. He said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, Masruq, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others said: it is what lies between the break of dawn (fajr) and the rising of the sun.

﴿And if He willed, He would have made it still⦆ meaning: constant, never moving away, as He said: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ and ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [al-Qasas: 71–72].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then We made the sun over it an indicator﴾ means: were it not for the sun rising upon it, the shadow would not be recognized, for opposites are known only through their opposites.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "an indicator" that follows it and pursues it until it covers all of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ refers to the shadow, and it was said: to the sun. ﴿Gradual﴾ means easy. Ibn 'Abbas said: swift. Mujahid said: hidden. Al-Suddi said: a hidden withdrawal, until no shadow remains on the earth except beneath a roof or beneath a tree, while the sun has already cast shade over what is above it.

Ayyub ibn Musa said: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ means: little by little.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He it is who made the night for you as a garment﴾ means: it covers and veils existence, as He said: [﴿By the night when it covers﴾ (al-Layl: 1)] and [﴿By the night when it covers it﴾ (al-Shams: 4)].

﴿And sleep as rest﴾ means: a cessation of movement for the rest of the bodies, for the limbs and members grow weary from much movement in dispersing by day in pursuit of livelihood. When night comes and stillness settles, the movements cease and rest is attained, so sleep occurs, in which there is rest for both body and spirit together.

﴿And made the day a resurrection﴾ means: people disperse in it for their livelihoods, their earnings, and their means, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas: 73].

﴿And made the day a resurrection﴾ means: people disperse in it for their livelihoods, their earnings, and their means, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas: 73].

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verses 45–47:

From here, Exalted is He, He began to explain the proofs that point to His existence and His complete power to create different and opposing things. He said: ﴿Have you not considered how your Lord extends the shadow?﴾ Ibn 'Abbas, Ibn 'Umar, Abu al-'Aliyah, Abu Malik, Masruq, Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Dahhak, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others said: it is what lies between the break of dawn (fajr) and the rising of the sun.

﴿And if He willed, He would have made it still⦆ meaning: constant, never moving away, as He said: ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the night perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ and ﴿Say: Have you considered, if Allah made the day perpetual over you until the Day of Resurrection...﴾ [al-Qasas: 71–72].

* *

His saying: ﴿Then We made the sun over it an indicator﴾ means: were it not for the sun rising upon it, the shadow would not be recognized, for opposites are known only through their opposites.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: "an indicator" that follows it and pursues it until it covers all of it.

* *

His saying: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ refers to the shadow, and it was said: to the sun. ﴿Gradual﴾ means easy. Ibn 'Abbas said: swift. Mujahid said: hidden. Al-Suddi said: a hidden withdrawal, until no shadow remains on the earth except beneath a roof or beneath a tree, while the sun has already cast shade over what is above it.

Ayyub ibn Musa said: ﴿Then We withdraw it to Us, a gradual withdrawal﴾ means: little by little.

* *

His saying: ﴿And He it is who made the night for you as a garment﴾ means: it covers and veils existence, as He said: [﴿By the night when it covers﴾ (al-Layl: 1)] and [﴿By the night when it covers it﴾ (al-Shams: 4)].

﴿And sleep as rest﴾ means: a cessation of movement for the rest of the bodies, for the limbs and members grow weary from much movement in dispersing by day in pursuit of livelihood. When night comes and stillness settles, the movements cease and rest is attained, so sleep occurs, in which there is rest for both body and spirit together.

﴿And made the day a resurrection﴾ means: people disperse in it for their livelihoods, their earnings, and their means, as Exalted is He said: ﴿And of His mercy, He made for you the night and the day, that you may rest therein and seek of His bounty, and perhaps you will be grateful﴾ [al-Qasas: 73].

This is also a sign of His perfect power and great dominion: He sends the winds as bearers of good news, meaning that they herald the coming of the clouds after them. The winds are of many kinds, with numerous characteristics of being subjected to God's command. Some raise the clouds, some carry them, some drive them, some go before the clouds as heralds of good news, some sweep the earth before that, and some fertilise the clouds so that they rain. For this reason He said: ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾, meaning a means by which one purifies oneself, like the *sahur* (the pre-dawn meal), the *waqud* (fuel), and what runs on their course. This is the most sound thing said about this. As for those who say that *tahur* is *fa'ul* in the sense of *fa'il*, or that it is formed for emphasis (*mubalaghah*) or transitivity (*ta'addi*), each of these views has problems from the standpoint of language and legal ruling. This is not the place to expand on them, and God knows best.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, from ʿUmar ibn Hafs ibn Ghiyath, who narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Jaʿfar al-Razi, from Humayd al-Tawil, from Thabit al-Bunani, who said: I entered with Abu al-ʿAliyah on a rainy day, when the roads of Basra were filthy, and he prayed. I asked him about it, and he said: ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾, and said: The rainwater purifies it.

He also said: My father narrated to us, who narrated to us, Abu Salamah narrated to us, Wuhayb narrated to us, from Dawud, from Saʿid ibn al-Musayyab regarding this verse: ﴿And We send down from the sky pure water﴾ [He said: God sent it down as pure water, which nothing makes impure.]

From Abu Saʿid, who said: It was said: "O Messenger of God, do we perform wudu' from the well of Buda'ah?" (It is a well into which filth and the flesh of dogs are thrown.) He said: "Indeed, water is pure and nothing makes it impure." Narrated by al-Shafiʿi and Ahmad, who graded it sound, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, who graded it good, and al-Nasa'i.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu al-Ashʿath narrated to us, Muʿtamir narrated to us, I heard my father narrate from Sayyar, from Khalid ibn Yazid, who said: He was with ʿAbd al-Malik ibn Marwan when they mentioned water. Khalid ibn Yazid said: Some of it comes from the sky, and some of it is what the cloud draws up from the sea, and thunder and lightning make it sweet. As for what comes from the sea, no plants grow from it; plants come only from what descends from the sky.

It is related from ʿIkrimah that he said: God does not send down a single drop from the sky without causing a plant to grow on the earth with it, or a pearl in the sea. Others said: On land it produces wheat, and in the sea it produces pearls.

* *

His saying: ﴿That We may give life thereby to a dead land﴾, meaning a land that has long awaited rain, so that it lies lifeless, with no plant or anything in it. When the rain reaches it, it comes to life, and its hills are clothed with all kinds of flowers and colours, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells and puts forth every lovely kind of growth﴾ [al-Hajj: 5].

﴿And that We may give drink to many of the cattle and humans whom We have created﴾, meaning that the animals, cattle and humans, may drink from it, being in extreme need of it for their drinking, their crops and their fruits, as He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And it is He who sends down the rain after they have despaired, and spreads His mercy, and He is the Protector, the Praiseworthy﴾ [al-Shura: 28]. And He said, may He be exalted: ﴿So look at the traces of God's mercy, how He gives life to the earth after its death. Surely that is the One who gives life to the dead, and He has power over all things﴾ [al-Rum: 50].

* *

His saying: ﴿And We have certainly distributed it among them that they may remember﴾, meaning: We sent rain upon this land and not that land, and We drove the clouds so that they passed over one land, went beyond it and crossed to another land. * *

As for His saying: ﴿And it is He who released the two seas, one sweet and palatable, and the other salty and bitter﴾, meaning: He created the two waters, the sweet and the salty. The sweet water is like the rivers, springs and wells, and this is the sweet, palatable, pure water. This was said by Ibn Jurayj, and chosen by Ibn Jarir, and this is beyond doubt, for there is no still body of water in existence that is sweet and palatable. God, glory be to Him, only reports what is actual [in A: "about the actual"] so that His servants may take heed of His blessings upon them and give thanks to Him. The sweet water is this flowing among the people, which God has distributed among His creatures, since they need it, as rivers and springs in every land, according to their need and their sufficiency for themselves and their lands.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and this is salty and bitter﴾, meaning: brackish, bitter, and undrinkable. This is like the well-known seas in the east and the west: the Ocean and what connects with it of inlets, the Red Sea [Bahr al-Qulzum], the Sea of Yemen, the Sea of Basra, the Persian Gulf, the seas of China and India, the Mediterranean, the Caspian Sea, and what resembles them and is similar to them of still seas that do not flow. Yet they surge, churn and become rough in winter and during strong winds. Some of them have tides and ebbs: at the beginning of every month they rise and swell, and when the month begins to wane they recede, until they return to their earliest limit. When the crescent of the next month appears, they begin to rise again until the fourteenth night, then they start to fall. God, glory be to Him, and to Him belongs complete power, established this custom. God, glory be to Him and exalted, created all these still seas with salty water, so that the air would not become foul because of them and the world would not be corrupted by that, and so that the earth would not be polluted by the animals that die in them. Since their water is salty, their air is wholesome and their dead are pure. For this reason the Messenger of God (ﷺ), when asked about sea water, "Shall we perform ablution with it?", said: "Its water is pure, and its carrion is lawful." It was narrated by the Imams Malik, al-Shafi'i, Ahmad, and the authors of the Sunan with a sound chain of transmission. [Its takhrij was previously mentioned under the commentary on verse 3 of Surah al-Ma'idah.]

* *

Ibn Kathir said:

Allah, the Exalted, informs us of the ignorance of the polytheists in worshipping other than Allah, namely the idols, which possess no power to benefit or harm them. They had no proof that led them to this, no argument that brought them to it, but only mere opinions, whims and desires. So they take them as allies, fight in their cause, and oppose Allah and His Messenger, [and the believers,] for their sake. Therefore He said: ﴿And the disbelievers are ever a helper [against] their Lord﴾, meaning, a supporter in the way of Satan against the party of Allah. The party of Allah are the victorious, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And they have taken gods other than Allah, hoping they might be helped. They are not able to help them, and they are [as] an army brought forward [to be punished]﴾ [Ya-Sin: 74–75], meaning: the gods they took besides Allah cannot give them any help, and these ignorant people are an army made ready for the idols, fighting on their behalf and defending their domain. But the final outcome and the victory belong to Allah and His Messenger, in this world and in the Hereafter.

Mujahid said regarding ﴿And the disbelievers are ever a helper [against] their Lord﴾: "He supports Satan in disobedience to Allah, assisting him."

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "[It means] an aide to Satan against his Lord, through enmity and shirk."

Zayd ibn Aslam said: "[It means] an ally."

Then Allah, the Exalted, said to His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a bringer of good tidings and a warner﴾, meaning, a bringer of good tidings to the believers and a warner to the disbelievers: bringing good news of Paradise to whoever obeys Allah, and warning of a severe punishment for whoever opposes the command of Allah.

﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any payment, except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 57] Meaning: for this message and this warning I do not ask you for any wage from your wealth; I only do it seeking the Face of Allah, ﴿for whoever among you wills to take the right course﴾ [At-Takwir: 28], ﴿except whoever wills to take to his Lord a way﴾, meaning, a path, a course and a method, to be followed by what I have brought.

Then He said: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾, meaning: in all your affairs, be one who relies upon Allah, the Ever-Living who never dies, the One who is ﴿the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾ [Al-Hadid: 3], the Everlasting, the Enduring, the Eternal, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Lord and Sovereign of everything. Make Him your treasure and your refuge. He is the One to be relied upon and the One to whom one turns for help, for He is sufficient for you, your Helper, your Supporter and your Victor, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Nufayl narrated to us, saying: I read to Ma'qil, meaning Ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Husayn, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Salman met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in one of the passages of Madinah, and he prostrated to him. He (ﷺ) said: "Do not prostrate to me, O Salman; prostrate instead to the Ever-Living who does not die." This is a *mursal* (a report in which the chain omits the Companion) but a good one. [It was also narrated by Abu Nu'aym in *Tarikh Asbahan* (2/103), through the route of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sayyar, from Hisham, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, with the same wording.]

[And His saying, ﴿And exalt Him with His praise﴾, meaning: combine His praise with His glorification.] This is why the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You," meaning: devote worship and reliance to Him sincerely, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9].

And He said: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123], and ﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 29].

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾, meaning: by His complete knowledge, nothing is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him.

And His saying: ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, meaning: He is the Ever-Living who does not die, the Creator of everything, its Lord and Sovereign, who by His power and authority created the seven heavens in their height and breadth, and the seven earths in their depth and density. ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: He manages the affair, decides the truth, and He is the best of judges.

﴿Say, "I do not ask you for it any payment, except that whoever wills may take to his Lord a way."﴾ [Al-Furqan: 57] Meaning: for this message and this warning I do not ask you for any wage from your wealth; I only do it seeking the Face of Allah, ﴿for whoever among you wills to take the right course﴾ [At-Takwir: 28], ﴿except whoever wills to take to his Lord a way﴾, meaning, a path, a course and a method, to be followed by what I have brought.

Then He said: ﴿And rely upon the Ever-Living who does not die﴾, meaning: in all your affairs, be one who relies upon Allah, the Ever-Living who never dies, the One who is ﴿the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾ [Al-Hadid: 3], the Everlasting, the Enduring, the Eternal, the Ever-Living, the Self-Subsisting, the Lord and Sovereign of everything. Make Him your treasure and your refuge. He is the One to be relied upon and the One to whom one turns for help, for He is sufficient for you, your Helper, your Supporter and your Victor, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Messenger, convey what has been revealed to you from your Lord. And if you do not, then you have not conveyed His message. And Allah will protect you from the people﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 67].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, saying: Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Nufayl narrated to us, saying: I read to Ma'qil, meaning Ibn Ubayd Allah, from Abdullah ibn Abi Husayn, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, who said: Salman met the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in one of the passages of Madinah, and he prostrated to him. He (ﷺ) said: "Do not prostrate to me, O Salman; prostrate instead to the Ever-Living who does not die." This is a *mursal* (a report in which the chain omits the Companion) but a good one. [It was also narrated by Abu Nu'aym in *Tarikh Asbahan* (2/103), through the route of Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Sayyar, from Hisham, from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Husayn, with the same wording.]

[And His saying, ﴿And exalt Him with His praise﴾, meaning: combine His praise with His glorification.] This is why the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: "Glory be to You, O Allah, our Lord, and praise be to You," meaning: devote worship and reliance to Him sincerely, as He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Lord of the east and the west; there is no deity except Him, so take Him as Disposer of affairs﴾ [Al-Muzzammil: 9].

And He said: ﴿So worship Him and rely upon Him﴾ [Hud: 123], and ﴿Say, "He is the Most Merciful; we have believed in Him and upon Him we have relied"﴾ [Al-Mulk: 29].

And His saying: ﴿And sufficient is He as Knower of the sins of His servants﴾, meaning: by His complete knowledge, nothing is hidden from Him, and not even the weight of an atom escapes Him.

And His saying: ﴿He who created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days﴾, meaning: He is the Ever-Living who does not die, the Creator of everything, its Lord and Sovereign, who by His power and authority created the seven heavens in their height and breadth, and the seven earths in their depth and density. ﴿Then He established Himself above the Throne, the Most Merciful﴾, meaning: He manages the affair, decides the truth, and He is the best of judges.

And His saying: ﴿Then established Himself on the Throne the Most Merciful; so ask about Him one who is informed﴾, meaning: inquire about Him from one who is well-informed and knowledgeable about Him, and follow him and take him as a model. It is known that there is no one more knowledgeable about Allah, nor more truthful about Him, than His servant and Messenger Muhammad, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, the master of all the descendants of Adam, in this world and the Hereafter, who ﴿does not speak from [his own] desire. It is not but a revelation revealed﴾ [An-Najm: 3–4]. Therefore, whatever he said is true, and whatever he reported is truth. He is the authoritative Imam, such that when people dispute about anything, their dispute must be referred to him. What agrees with his sayings and actions is the truth, and what opposes them is rejected, whoever says or does it, whoever he may be. Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And if you disagree over anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 59].

He also said: ﴿And whatever you differ over, its ruling is with Allah﴾ [Ash-Shura: 10], and He, the Exalted, said: ﴿And the word of your Lord has been fulfilled in truth and justice﴾ [Al-An'am: 115], meaning: truthful in what He reports and just in His commands and prohibitions. This is why He said: ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾.

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾: "Whatever I inform you of is exactly as I have informed you." Ibn Jurayj said likewise.

Shimr ibn Atiyyah said regarding His saying ﴿So ask about Him one who is informed﴾: "This Qur'an is the one informed about Him."

Then Allah, the Exalted, said, rebuking the polytheists who prostrate to other than Allah, to idols and rivals: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful? Shall we prostrate to what you command us?"﴾ and it increases them in aversion [Al-Furqan: 60]. That is, they say: "We do not know the Most Merciful." They used to deny that Allah could be named by His name "the Most Merciful," just as they denied this on the day of Hudaybiyyah, when the Prophet (ﷺ) said to the scribe: "Write: In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate." They said: "We do not know 'the Most Merciful' or 'the Most Compassionate'; rather, write as you used to write: 'In Your name, O Allah.'" For this reason Allah revealed: ﴿Say, "Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the best names"﴾ [Al-Isra: 110], meaning: He is Allah and He is the Most Merciful. And in this verse He said: ﴿And when it is said to them, "Prostrate to the Most Merciful," they say, "And what is the Most Merciful?"﴾, meaning: we do not recognise Him and we do not acknowledge Him? ﴿Shall we prostrate to what you command us?﴾, meaning: merely because of your word? ﴿And it increases them in aversion﴾. As for the believers, they worship Allah, who is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, and they single Him out with divinity and prostrate to Him. The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, have agreed that the prostration in Surah Al-Furqan is one at which it is prescribed for its reciter and its listener to prostrate, as is established in its proper place. And Allah knows best.

Allah, the Exalted, says, glorifying Himself and magnifying Himself for the beauty of what He created in the sky of the *burūj* (constellations). According to the saying of Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, al-Hasan and Qatadah, these are the great stars.

It has also been said that they are palaces in the sky for the guards (*ḥaras*). This is narrated from 'Ali, Ibn 'Abbas, Muhammad ibn Ka'b, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash. It is also a narration from Abu Salih. The first opinion, however, is more apparent. Unless the great stars are themselves palaces for the guards, in which case the two opinions come together, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We have adorned the lowest heaven with lamps, and made them missiles against the devils﴾ [al-Mulk: 5]. For this reason He said: ﴿Blessed is He who placed in the sky constellations and placed therein a lamp﴾, meaning the shining sun, which is like a lamp in existence, as He said: ﴿And We made a blazing lamp﴾ [al-Naba': 13].

﴿And a moon giving light﴾, i.e., shining and radiant with another light and a different kind and form, other than the light of the sun, as He said: ﴿He it is who made the sun a radiance and the moon a light﴾ [Yunus: 5]. And He related, concerning Nuh, peace be upon him, that he said to his people: ﴿Have you not considered how Allah created seven heavens in layers, and made the moon therein a light and made the sun a lamp?﴾ [Nuh: 15–16].

Then He said: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day alternating﴾, meaning each of them succeeds the other, they follow one another without ceasing. When this one goes, that one comes, and when that one comes, this one goes, as He said: ﴿And He subjected for you the sun and the moon, both continuing [in their courses], and subjected for you the night and the day﴾ [Ibrahim: 33]; and He said: ﴿He covers the night with the day, which pursues it swiftly, and the sun and the moon and the stars [are] subjected by His command﴾ [al-A'raf: 54]; and He said: ﴿It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor does the night outstrip the day, but each [celestial body] is travelling in an orbit﴾ [Ya-Sin: 40].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful﴾, meaning: He made the two succeed each other as a timing for His servants' worship of Him. Whoever misses a deed at night makes it up during the day, and whoever misses a deed during the day makes it up at night. It has come in the authentic hadith: "Indeed Allah, the Exalted, extends His hand by night so that the one who sinned by day may repent, and extends His hand by day so that the one who sinned by night may repent" [[Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih, no. (2759), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Abu Hurrah narrated to us from al-Hasan that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab prolonged the Duha prayer. He was asked: "Today you did something you would not normally do?" He said: "There remained some of my portion (of worship), so I wished to complete it, or he said: to fulfil it," and he recited this verse: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day alternating [for whoever wishes to remember or wishes to be grateful]﴾ [[This report is disconnected (munqati'), for al-Hasan did not hear from 'Umar.]].

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, concerning His saying: ﴿And He it is who made the night and the day alternating﴾, that he said: "Whoever misses something of the night that he should do, he makes it up by day, or of the day he makes it up by night." Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Hasan said likewise.

Mujahid and Qatadah said: ﴿khilfah﴾ means differing from one another: this one in its darkness, and this one in its light.

Allah, the Exalted, says, glorifying Himself and magnifying Himself for the beauty of what He created in the sky of the *burūj* (constellations). According to the saying of Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu Salih, al-Hasan and Qatadah, these are the great stars.
