The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn Yahya related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Maymun related to us, Sa'id ibn Hakim related to us, from Muslim ibn Habib, from Bilal, that is al-Absi, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How excellent is moderation in wealth, and how excellent is moderation in poverty, and how excellent is moderation in worship." Then he said: We do not know it being related except from the hadith of Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 3604; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/252): "Al-Bazzar related it from Sa'id ibn Hakim from Muslim ibn Habib; this Muslim I have not found mentioned by anyone except Ibn Hibban in the biography of Sa'id, the narrator from him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: Whatever you exceed the command of Allah with is extravagance (israf).

Others said: Extravagance is spending in disobedience to Allah.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Spending in the way of Allah is not extravagance. [And Allah knows best.]

This is the description of the believing servants of Allah. ﴿Those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, that is, with tranquility and dignity, without arrogance or haughtiness, as He said: ﴿And do not walk upon the earth exultantly; indeed, you will not tear the earth apart, and you will not reach the mountains in height﴾ [Al-Isra: 37]. As for these, they walk without pride, without exultation, without insolence or boastfulness. The intended meaning is not that they walk like the sick, affecting weakness as a show and for display. The master of the children of Adam ﷺ, when he walked, seemed to be descending from a slope, and it was as if the earth were folded up for him. Some of the early generations (al-salaf) disliked walking with feigned weakness and affectation, to the point that it is related from Umar that he saw a young man walking slowly, and said: "What is the matter with you? Are you ill?" He said: "No, O Commander of the Believers." So Umar struck him with his whip and ordered him to walk with vigour. The meaning of hawn (humility) here is tranquility and dignity, as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When you come to the prayer, do not come to it running; come to it walking calmly with tranquility. Pray what you catch up with, and complete what you have missed." [Reported by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 635, and Muslim in his Sahih, no. 603, from the hadith of Abu Qatadah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said, from Ma'mar, from Yahya ibn al-Mukhtar, from al-Hasan al-Basri, concerning His words: ﴿And the servants of the Most Merciful are those who walk upon the earth in humility﴾, he said: "The believers are a humble people. By Allah, their hearing, their sight and their limbs are humbled, so that you think they are sick, while the people are not sick; rather, they are healthy. But fear has entered them as it has not entered others, and their knowledge of the Hereafter has kept them from the world. They say: 'Praise be to Allah who has removed sorrow from us.' By Allah, the sorrow of the people has not saddened them, and nothing that they sought the Garden by has seemed great in their souls. The fear of the Fire has made them weep. Whoever is not consoled by the consolation of Allah, his soul will break in regret over the world, and whoever does not see the blessing of Allah except in food or drink, his knowledge has become little and his punishment has been made present."

* *

His words: ﴿And when the ignorant address them, they say: "Peace."﴾ That is, when the foolish treat them with evil, they do not repay them in kind; rather, they pardon and overlook, and say nothing but good. Just as the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, the intensity of ignorance directed at him increased him only in forbearance. And as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And when they hear idle talk, they turn away from it and say: "To us our deeds, and to you your deeds. Peace be upon you; we do not seek the ignorant."﴾ [Al-Qasas: 55].

Imam Ahmad said: Aswad ibn Amir related to us, Abu Bakr related to us, from al-A'mash, from Abu Khalid al-Walibi, from al-Nu'man ibn Muqarrin al-Muzani, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and a man abused another man in his presence. The abused man began to say: "Peace be upon you." So the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, an angel between you two defends you. Whenever this one abuses you, he says to him: 'Rather, you, and you are more deserving of it.' And when he says to him: 'Peace be upon you,' he says: 'No, rather upon you, and you are more deserving of it.'" Its chain is good (hasan), and they did not record it. [Al-Musnad (5/445), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/75): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih, except Abu Khalid al-Walibi, who is trustworthy."]

Mujahid said: ﴿They say "Peace"﴾ means they say: "Sadadan" (rightness, a sound word).

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: They return a good word.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿They say "Peace"﴾: they are forbearing, not ignorant, and if ignorance is directed at them, they are patient. They keep company with the servants of Allah by day, with what you hear (in their words), then he mentioned that their night is the best of nights.

* *

His words: ﴿And those who spend the night before their Lord, prostrating and standing﴾, that is, in His worship and obedience, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿They used to sleep little of the night, and at dawn they would seek forgiveness﴾ [Adh-Dhariyat: 17-18]. And He said: ﴿Their sides forsake their beds, calling upon their Lord in fear and hope, and from what We have provided them they spend﴾ [As-Sajdah: 16]. And He said: ﴿Is one who worships devoutly during the hours of the night, prostrating and standing, fearing the Hereafter and hoping for the mercy of his Lord...﴾ [Az-Zumar: 9]. Therefore He said: ﴿And those who say: "Our Lord, avert from us the punishment of Hell; indeed, its punishment is ever-adhering (gharaman)"﴾, that is, constant and enduring, as the poet said:

"If it punishes, it is gharaman, and if it gives, it gives abundantly, and it does not care."

Therefore al-Hasan said concerning His words: ﴿Indeed, its punishment was gharaman﴾: Everything that afflicts the son of Adam and then departs from him is not gharam; rather, gharam is that which is lasting for as long as the heavens and the earth endure. Sulayman al-Taymi said likewise.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: ﴿Indeed, its punishment was gharaman﴾, meaning: what they enjoyed in the world. Allah asked the disbelievers about the blessing, and they did not return it to Him, so He made them liable for it (aghramahum), and He admitted them into the Fire.

﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and a station﴾, that is, evil is the dwelling as a place to be seen, and evil is the resting place as a station.

Ibn Abi Hatim said, concerning His words ﴿Indeed, it is evil as a place of settlement and a station﴾: My father related to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' related to us, Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from al-A'mash, from Malik ibn al-Harith, who said: When a man is thrown into the Fire, he falls into it, and when he reaches one of its gates, it is said to him: "Stay where you are until you are presented with a gift." He said: So he is given a cup of the poison of vipers and scorpions. He said: Then the skin is separated from him, and the hair separately, and the sinews separately, and the veins separately.

He also said: My father related to us, al-Hasan ibn al-Rabi' related to us, Abu al-Ahwas related to us, from al-A'mash, from Mujahid, from Ubayd ibn Umayr, who said: Indeed, in the Fire there are pits in which there are serpents the size of Bactrian camels and scorpions the size of dark mules. When they are cast into the Fire, these creatures come out to them from their dwellings and seize their lips, their skins and their hair, and they strip their flesh down to their feet. When they feel the heat of the Fire, they return.

Imam Ahmad said: al-Hasan ibn Musa related to us, Sallam, that is Ibn Miskin, related to us, from Abu Zilal, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Indeed, a servant in Hell will call out for a thousand years: 'O Hannan! O Mannan!' Then Allah says to Jibril: 'Go and bring Me this servant of Mine.' Jibril goes and finds the people of the Fire prostrate, weeping, so he returns to his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and informs Him. Allah says: 'Bring him to Me, for he is in such-and-such a place.' So he brings him and stands him before his Lord, the Mighty and Majestic, and He says to him: 'O My servant, how did you find your place and your resting place?' He says: 'O my Lord, the worst of places, the worst of resting places.' He says: 'Return My servant.' He says: 'O my Lord, I did not hope, when You brought me out of it, that You would return me to it!' He says: 'Leave My servant alone.'" [Al-Musnad (3/230), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/384): "Its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih except Abu Zilal, whom most scholars considered weak, while Ibn Hibban considered him trustworthy."]

* *

His words: ﴿And those who, when they spend, are neither extravagant nor stingy, but are between that moderate﴾, that is, they are not wasteful in their spending, spending beyond need, nor are they miserly toward their families, falling short in their rights so that they do not suffice them; rather, they are just and choice. The best of matters is their middle, neither this nor that. ﴿And was between that a stand (qawaman)﴾, as He said: ﴿And do not make your hand chained to your neck, nor extend it fully outstretched, lest you sit reproached and destitute﴾ [Al-Isra: 29].

Imam Ahmad said: Isam ibn Khalid related to us, Abu Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Maryam al-Ghassani related to me, from Damrah, from Abu al-Darda', from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "Part of a man's understanding (fiqh) is his gentleness in his livelihood." They did not record it. [Al-Musnad (5/194).]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Ubaydah al-Haddad related to us, Sukayn ibn Abd al-Aziz al-Abdi related to us, Ibrahim al-Hajari related to us, from Abu al-Ahwas, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "No one becomes poor who is moderate." They did not record it. [Al-Musnad (1/447), and al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/252): "Its chain includes Ibrahim ibn Muslim al-Hajari, who is weak."]

The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn Yahya related to us, Ibrahim ibn Muhammad ibn Maymun related to us, Sa'id ibn Hakim related to us, from Muslim ibn Habib, from Bilal, that is al-Absi, from Hudhayfah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "How excellent is moderation in wealth, and how excellent is moderation in poverty, and how excellent is moderation in worship." Then he said: We do not know it being related except from the hadith of Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 3604; al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/252): "Al-Bazzar related it from Sa'id ibn Hakim from Muslim ibn Habib; this Muslim I have not found mentioned by anyone except Ibn Hibban in the biography of Sa'id, the narrator from him, and the rest of its narrators are trustworthy."]

Iyas ibn Mu'awiyah said: Whatever you exceed the command of Allah with is extravagance (israf).

Others said: Extravagance is spending in disobedience to Allah.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Spending in the way of Allah is not extravagance. [And Allah knows best.]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah – that is, Ibn Mas'ud – who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which sin is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that it will eat with you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." 'Abdullah said: And Allah revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit adultery – and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same chain (al-Musnad (1/380) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11368)).

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash and Mansur – al-Bukhari added: and Wasil – all three from Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)). Allah knows best. The wording of both on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud is: He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" – and the hadith continues.

A gharib route: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, 'Amir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, al-Sari – meaning Ibn Isma'il – narrated to us, al-Sha'bi narrated to us, from Masruq who said: 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day and I followed him. He sat on a raised ground, and I sat below him, my face level with his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, which of the sins is greatest?" He said: "That you call upon a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ to the end of the verse (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)).

Al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Salamah ibn Qays who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily there are only four – I am not more miserly with them since I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Do not associate anything with Allah; do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right; do not commit adultery; and do not steal" (al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11373)).

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, I heard Abu Tayba al-Kala'i, I heard al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "What do you say about fornication (zina)?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said to his companions: "For a man to commit adultery with ten women is easier for him than to commit adultery with the wife of his neighbour." He said: "What do you say about theft?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden. He said: "For a man to steal from ten houses is easier for him than to steal from his neighbour" (al-Musnad (6/8); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/168): "its narrators are trustworthy").

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: 'Ammar ibn Nasr narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no sin after shirk greater in the sight of Allah than a drop of semen which a man places in a womb that is not lawful for him" (al-Wara' of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. (137): "It is mursal, and in its chain is Baqiyyah, who is a mudallis, and Ibn Abi Maryam is weak," as derived from the words of the esteemed scholar Muhammad al-Hamud).

Ibn Jurayj said: Yala informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard him narrate from Ibn 'Abbas: that some people from the people of shirk had killed and killed much, and committed adultery and committed much, then they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good; if only you would inform us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu Fakhitah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah forbids you to worship the created and to abandon the Creator, and He forbids you to kill your child and feed your dog, and He forbids you to commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Sufyan said: This is His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾ (al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/277) and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim. It appears there as "from Abu Qatadah"; if that is so it is connected (mawsul), but if it is as stated here, it is mursal, and I have not clarified which of the two is correct, Allah knows best).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that he said: "Athaman" is a valley in Hell.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means valleys in Hell in which adulterers are punished. The same was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

Qatadah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means a punishment. We used to narrate that it is a valley in Hell.

It has been mentioned to us that Luqman used to say: "O my son, beware of adultery, for its beginning is fear and its end is regret."

It has also appeared in the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir and others, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili – both mawquf and marfu' – that "Ghayy" and "Athaman" are two wells at the bottom of Hell (Tafsir al-Tabari (19/29)). May Allah save us from them by His bounty and generosity.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: a recompense.

This is more apparent in the verse's outward meaning; for this reason it is explained by what follows it as a substitute: His saying: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning it will be repeated upon him and made more severe, ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾, meaning abased and degraded.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds﴾ – meaning: his recompense for what he did of these ugly attributes is what has been mentioned, ﴿except one who repents﴾ in this world to Allah from all of that, for indeed Allah accepts his repentance.

In this is evidence for the validity of the repentance of the murderer. There is no contradiction between this and the verse of an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 93]. For although this is Medinan, it is unrestricted, so it is understood as applying to one who does not repent, since that one is restricted by repentance. Then Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa': 48, 116].

The authentic Sunnah has established, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the validity of the repentance of the murderer, as is mentioned confirmed in the story of the one who killed one hundred men and then repented, and it was accepted from him, along with other hadiths.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾: regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ there are two opinions.

The first: that they are substituted, in place of performing evil deeds, with performing good deeds. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ that he said: They are the believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; then Allah turned away from that concerning them and transferred them to good deeds, replacing evil deeds with good deeds for them.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite, at this verse, the lines:

"They were changed after their heat into autumn, and after the long breath, the panting."

meaning: those states were changed into other states.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: This is in this world: a man is in an ugly condition, then Allah replaces it for him with something better.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He replaced for them the worship of idols with the worship of Allah; and He replaced for them fighting the Muslims with fighting alongside the Muslims against the polytheists; and He replaced for them marrying polytheist women with marrying believing women.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah replaced for them evil action with righteous action, shirk with sincerity, immorality with chastity, and disbelief with Islam.

This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, and a group of others.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed by sincere repentance itself into good deeds; and this is only because whenever he recalls what has passed, he regrets, seeks forgiveness and asks for forgiveness, so the sin becomes an act of obedience in this respect. On the Day of Resurrection, even if he finds it written against him, it will not harm him, and it will turn into a good deed in his record, as the Sunnah has established regarding this, and the narrations transmitted from the early generations (salaf), may Allah have mercy on them, have been authenticated with it. This is the context of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise: a man will be brought and it will be said: Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones. It will be said to him: 'On such and such a day you did such and such, and on such and such a day you did such and such?' He will say: 'Yes' – he cannot deny any of it – and it will be said: 'For you, for every evil deed there is a good deed.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things which I do not see here.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed. Muslim alone narrated it (al-Musnad (5/170) and Sahih Muslim, no. (190)).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam sleeps, the angel says to the devil: 'Give me your record.' He gives it to him, and whatever good deed he finds in his record, he erases ten evil deeds from the devil's record and writes them as good deeds. So when one of you wants to sleep, let him say Allahu Akbar thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-four times, and glorify Allah thirty-three times – that is one hundred" (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/296); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/121): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, who is weak," and his hearing from his father is also not established).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah and 'Arim narrated to us, both said: Thabit – meaning Ibn Yazid Abu Zayd – narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman who said: A man will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection and will read its top; there are his evil deeds, and when his assessment nearly turns bad, he looks at its bottom and there are his good deeds; then he looks again at its top and behold, it has been changed into good deeds.

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abu al-Anbas narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will surely bring forth people on the Day of Resurrection who thought they had accumulated many misdeeds." It was said: "Who are they, O Abu Hurayrah?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah will replace with good deeds."

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Dayf, who was one of the companions of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise in four categories: the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), then the grateful (al-shakirin), then those who fear (al-khaifin), then the companions of the right hand (ashab al-yamin)." I said: "Why were they called the companions of the right hand?" He said: "Because they did good deeds and evil deeds. Their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will read their evil deeds letter by letter. They will say: 'O our Lord, these are our evil deeds, so where are our good deeds?' At that moment Allah will erase the evil deeds and turn them into good deeds. Then they will say: ﴿Here, read my book!﴾ [69:19]. They are the majority of the people of Paradise."

Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin said regarding ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾: "This is in the Hereafter."

Makhul said: "He will forgive them and make them good deeds." [Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both of these, and Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abu Jabir narrated to us, that he heard Makhul narrating, who said: "An old man, very aged, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man who betrayed and committed immorality, leaving no need or small matter without seizing it with his right hand. If his sin were divided among the people of the earth, it would destroy them. Is there repentance for him?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: 'Have you embraced Islam?' He said: 'As for me, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed Allah will forgive you for what you did before, and will replace your evil deeds with good deeds.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and my betrayals and my immoralities?' He said: 'And your betrayals and your immoralities.' Then the man turned away, saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' and 'Allahu akbar'."

[Ahmad al-Imam connected this in his Musnad (4/384) through the route of Nuh ibn Qays, from Ashath ibn Jabir al-Hudani, from Makhul, from Amr ibn Absah, with it being marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), abridged at its beginning and end. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/32): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that it is a narration of Makhul from Amr ibn Absah, so I do not know whether he heard it from him or not."]

Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu Farwah (Shatab), that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What do you say about a man who committed all sins and left no need or small matter? Is there repentance for him?" He said: "Have you embraced Islam?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then do the good deeds, and leave the evil deeds, and Allah will turn them all into good deeds for you." He said: "And my betrayals and my immoralities?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he kept saying 'Allahu akbar' until he disappeared from view."

[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/314); al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (3/352) through the route of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi, from Abu al-Mughirah with the same chain. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: "Other than Muhammad ibn Harun narrated this hadith from Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ..., (tawil shatab al-mamdud), and I think Muhammad ibn Harun made a mistake in it, and the correct version is what others have said."]

It was also narrated by al-Tabarani through the route of Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, from Yasin al-Zayyat, from Abu Salamah al-Himsi, from Yahya ibn Jabir, from Salamah ibn Nufayl, as a marfu' hadith. [Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/53). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Yasin al-Zayyat, who narrates fabricated (mawdu'at) reports."]

And he also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Isa ibn Shu'ayb ibn Thawban narrated to us, from Fulayh al-Shammas, from Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A woman came to me and said: 'Is there repentance for me? I committed fornication, gave birth, and killed the child.' I said: 'No, and may the eye not be pleased, and there is no honor for you.' So she stood up, calling out in grief. Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and I related to him what the woman had said and what I had said to her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Evil is what you said! Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah...﴾ up to His words: ﴿except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [25:68–70]?' So I recited it to her. Then she fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me.'"

This is a strange hadith (gharib) through this route, and among its narrators is one who is not known; and Allah knows best. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami with his chain, in similar wording, and in his version: "She went out calling in grief and saying: 'Alas for my grief! Was this beauty created for the Fire?' In his version also, when he returned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he searched for her in all the houses of Madinah and did not find her. When the following night came, she came to him, and he informed her of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to him. She fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me and repentance from what I did.' She freed a slave girl who was with her, and her daughter, and she repented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/27); Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/279), and al-Suyuti said: "Its chain is weak."]

Then He, exalted is He, said, informing about the comprehensiveness of His mercy toward His servants, and that whoever among them turns to Him in repentance, He will accept his repentance, regardless of what sin it was, whether grave or trivial, great or small: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, then indeed he turns to Allah with a true turning﴾ [25:71], meaning: indeed Allah accepts his repentance, just as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [4:110]; and He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charity, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾ [9:104]; and He said: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [39:53], meaning: for whoever repents to Him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah – that is, Ibn Mas'ud – who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which sin is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that it will eat with you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." 'Abdullah said: And Allah revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit adultery – and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same chain (al-Musnad (1/380) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11368)).

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash and Mansur – al-Bukhari added: and Wasil – all three from Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)). Allah knows best. The wording of both on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud is: He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" – and the hadith continues.

A gharib route: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, 'Amir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, al-Sari – meaning Ibn Isma'il – narrated to us, al-Sha'bi narrated to us, from Masruq who said: 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day and I followed him. He sat on a raised ground, and I sat below him, my face level with his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, which of the sins is greatest?" He said: "That you call upon a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ to the end of the verse (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)).

Al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Salamah ibn Qays who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily there are only four – I am not more miserly with them since I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Do not associate anything with Allah; do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right; do not commit adultery; and do not steal" (al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11373)).

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, I heard Abu Tayba al-Kala'i, I heard al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "What do you say about fornication (zina)?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said to his companions: "For a man to commit adultery with ten women is easier for him than to commit adultery with the wife of his neighbour." He said: "What do you say about theft?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden. He said: "For a man to steal from ten houses is easier for him than to steal from his neighbour" (al-Musnad (6/8); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/168): "its narrators are trustworthy").

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: 'Ammar ibn Nasr narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no sin after shirk greater in the sight of Allah than a drop of semen which a man places in a womb that is not lawful for him" (al-Wara' of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. (137): "It is mursal, and in its chain is Baqiyyah, who is a mudallis, and Ibn Abi Maryam is weak," as derived from the words of the esteemed scholar Muhammad al-Hamud).

Ibn Jurayj said: Yala informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard him narrate from Ibn 'Abbas: that some people from the people of shirk had killed and killed much, and committed adultery and committed much, then they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good; if only you would inform us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu Fakhitah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah forbids you to worship the created and to abandon the Creator, and He forbids you to kill your child and feed your dog, and He forbids you to commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Sufyan said: This is His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾ (al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/277) and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim. It appears there as "from Abu Qatadah"; if that is so it is connected (mawsul), but if it is as stated here, it is mursal, and I have not clarified which of the two is correct, Allah knows best).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that he said: "Athaman" is a valley in Hell.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means valleys in Hell in which adulterers are punished. The same was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

Qatadah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means a punishment. We used to narrate that it is a valley in Hell.

It has been mentioned to us that Luqman used to say: "O my son, beware of adultery, for its beginning is fear and its end is regret."

It has also appeared in the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir and others, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili – both mawquf and marfu' – that "Ghayy" and "Athaman" are two wells at the bottom of Hell (Tafsir al-Tabari (19/29)). May Allah save us from them by His bounty and generosity.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: a recompense.

This is more apparent in the verse's outward meaning; for this reason it is explained by what follows it as a substitute: His saying: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning it will be repeated upon him and made more severe, ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾, meaning abased and degraded.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds﴾ – meaning: his recompense for what he did of these ugly attributes is what has been mentioned, ﴿except one who repents﴾ in this world to Allah from all of that, for indeed Allah accepts his repentance.

In this is evidence for the validity of the repentance of the murderer. There is no contradiction between this and the verse of an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 93]. For although this is Medinan, it is unrestricted, so it is understood as applying to one who does not repent, since that one is restricted by repentance. Then Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa': 48, 116].

The authentic Sunnah has established, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the validity of the repentance of the murderer, as is mentioned confirmed in the story of the one who killed one hundred men and then repented, and it was accepted from him, along with other hadiths.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾: regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ there are two opinions.

The first: that they are substituted, in place of performing evil deeds, with performing good deeds. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ that he said: They are the believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; then Allah turned away from that concerning them and transferred them to good deeds, replacing evil deeds with good deeds for them.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite, at this verse, the lines:

"They were changed after their heat into autumn, and after the long breath, the panting."

meaning: those states were changed into other states.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: This is in this world: a man is in an ugly condition, then Allah replaces it for him with something better.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He replaced for them the worship of idols with the worship of Allah; and He replaced for them fighting the Muslims with fighting alongside the Muslims against the polytheists; and He replaced for them marrying polytheist women with marrying believing women.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah replaced for them evil action with righteous action, shirk with sincerity, immorality with chastity, and disbelief with Islam.

This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, and a group of others.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed by sincere repentance itself into good deeds; and this is only because whenever he recalls what has passed, he regrets, seeks forgiveness and asks for forgiveness, so the sin becomes an act of obedience in this respect. On the Day of Resurrection, even if he finds it written against him, it will not harm him, and it will turn into a good deed in his record, as the Sunnah has established regarding this, and the narrations transmitted from the early generations (salaf), may Allah have mercy on them, have been authenticated with it. This is the context of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise: a man will be brought and it will be said: Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones. It will be said to him: 'On such and such a day you did such and such, and on such and such a day you did such and such?' He will say: 'Yes' – he cannot deny any of it – and it will be said: 'For you, for every evil deed there is a good deed.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things which I do not see here.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed. Muslim alone narrated it (al-Musnad (5/170) and Sahih Muslim, no. (190)).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam sleeps, the angel says to the devil: 'Give me your record.' He gives it to him, and whatever good deed he finds in his record, he erases ten evil deeds from the devil's record and writes them as good deeds. So when one of you wants to sleep, let him say Allahu Akbar thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-four times, and glorify Allah thirty-three times – that is one hundred" (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/296); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/121): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, who is weak," and his hearing from his father is also not established).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah and 'Arim narrated to us, both said: Thabit – meaning Ibn Yazid Abu Zayd – narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman who said: A man will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection and will read its top; there are his evil deeds, and when his assessment nearly turns bad, he looks at its bottom and there are his good deeds; then he looks again at its top and behold, it has been changed into good deeds.

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abu al-Anbas narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will surely bring forth people on the Day of Resurrection who thought they had accumulated many misdeeds." It was said: "Who are they, O Abu Hurayrah?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah will replace with good deeds."

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Dayf, who was one of the companions of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise in four categories: the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), then the grateful (al-shakirin), then those who fear (al-khaifin), then the companions of the right hand (ashab al-yamin)." I said: "Why were they called the companions of the right hand?" He said: "Because they did good deeds and evil deeds. Their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will read their evil deeds letter by letter. They will say: 'O our Lord, these are our evil deeds, so where are our good deeds?' At that moment Allah will erase the evil deeds and turn them into good deeds. Then they will say: ﴿Here, read my book!﴾ [69:19]. They are the majority of the people of Paradise."

Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin said regarding ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾: "This is in the Hereafter."

Makhul said: "He will forgive them and make them good deeds." [Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both of these, and Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abu Jabir narrated to us, that he heard Makhul narrating, who said: "An old man, very aged, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man who betrayed and committed immorality, leaving no need or small matter without seizing it with his right hand. If his sin were divided among the people of the earth, it would destroy them. Is there repentance for him?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: 'Have you embraced Islam?' He said: 'As for me, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed Allah will forgive you for what you did before, and will replace your evil deeds with good deeds.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and my betrayals and my immoralities?' He said: 'And your betrayals and your immoralities.' Then the man turned away, saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' and 'Allahu akbar'."

[Ahmad al-Imam connected this in his Musnad (4/384) through the route of Nuh ibn Qays, from Ashath ibn Jabir al-Hudani, from Makhul, from Amr ibn Absah, with it being marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), abridged at its beginning and end. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/32): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that it is a narration of Makhul from Amr ibn Absah, so I do not know whether he heard it from him or not."]

Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu Farwah (Shatab), that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What do you say about a man who committed all sins and left no need or small matter? Is there repentance for him?" He said: "Have you embraced Islam?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then do the good deeds, and leave the evil deeds, and Allah will turn them all into good deeds for you." He said: "And my betrayals and my immoralities?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he kept saying 'Allahu akbar' until he disappeared from view."

[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/314); al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (3/352) through the route of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi, from Abu al-Mughirah with the same chain. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: "Other than Muhammad ibn Harun narrated this hadith from Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ..., (tawil shatab al-mamdud), and I think Muhammad ibn Harun made a mistake in it, and the correct version is what others have said."]

It was also narrated by al-Tabarani through the route of Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, from Yasin al-Zayyat, from Abu Salamah al-Himsi, from Yahya ibn Jabir, from Salamah ibn Nufayl, as a marfu' hadith. [Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/53). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Yasin al-Zayyat, who narrates fabricated (mawdu'at) reports."]

And he also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Isa ibn Shu'ayb ibn Thawban narrated to us, from Fulayh al-Shammas, from Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A woman came to me and said: 'Is there repentance for me? I committed fornication, gave birth, and killed the child.' I said: 'No, and may the eye not be pleased, and there is no honor for you.' So she stood up, calling out in grief. Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and I related to him what the woman had said and what I had said to her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Evil is what you said! Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah...﴾ up to His words: ﴿except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [25:68–70]?' So I recited it to her. Then she fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me.'"

This is a strange hadith (gharib) through this route, and among its narrators is one who is not known; and Allah knows best. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami with his chain, in similar wording, and in his version: "She went out calling in grief and saying: 'Alas for my grief! Was this beauty created for the Fire?' In his version also, when he returned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he searched for her in all the houses of Madinah and did not find her. When the following night came, she came to him, and he informed her of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to him. She fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me and repentance from what I did.' She freed a slave girl who was with her, and her daughter, and she repented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/27); Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/279), and al-Suyuti said: "Its chain is weak."]

Then He, exalted is He, said, informing about the comprehensiveness of His mercy toward His servants, and that whoever among them turns to Him in repentance, He will accept his repentance, regardless of what sin it was, whether grave or trivial, great or small: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, then indeed he turns to Allah with a true turning﴾ [25:71], meaning: indeed Allah accepts his repentance, just as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [4:110]; and He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charity, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾ [9:104]; and He said: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [39:53], meaning: for whoever repents to Him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah – that is, Ibn Mas'ud – who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which sin is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that it will eat with you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." 'Abdullah said: And Allah revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit adultery – and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same chain (al-Musnad (1/380) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11368)).

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash and Mansur – al-Bukhari added: and Wasil – all three from Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)). Allah knows best. The wording of both on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud is: He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" – and the hadith continues.

A gharib route: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, 'Amir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, al-Sari – meaning Ibn Isma'il – narrated to us, al-Sha'bi narrated to us, from Masruq who said: 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day and I followed him. He sat on a raised ground, and I sat below him, my face level with his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, which of the sins is greatest?" He said: "That you call upon a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ to the end of the verse (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)).

Al-Nasa'i said: Qutaybah ibn Sa'id narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mansur, from Hilal ibn Yasaf, from Salamah ibn Qays who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said during the Farewell Pilgrimage: "Verily there are only four – I am not more miserly with them since I heard them from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): Do not associate anything with Allah; do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right; do not commit adultery; and do not steal" (al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11373)).

Imam Ahmad said: 'Ali ibn al-Madini, may Allah have mercy on him, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Fudayl ibn Ghazwan narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Sa'd al-Ansari narrated to us, I heard Abu Tayba al-Kala'i, I heard al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah be pleased with him, say: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to his companions: "What do you say about fornication (zina)?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden until the Day of Resurrection. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then said to his companions: "For a man to commit adultery with ten women is easier for him than to commit adultery with the wife of his neighbour." He said: "What do you say about theft?" They said: Allah and His Messenger have forbidden it, so it is forbidden. He said: "For a man to steal from ten houses is easier for him than to steal from his neighbour" (al-Musnad (6/8); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/168): "its narrators are trustworthy").

Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Dunya said: 'Ammar ibn Nasr narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Maryam, from al-Haytham ibn Malik al-Ta'i, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There is no sin after shirk greater in the sight of Allah than a drop of semen which a man places in a womb that is not lawful for him" (al-Wara' of Ibn Abi al-Dunya, no. (137): "It is mursal, and in its chain is Baqiyyah, who is a mudallis, and Ibn Abi Maryam is weak," as derived from the words of the esteemed scholar Muhammad al-Hamud).

Ibn Jurayj said: Yala informed me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, that he heard him narrate from Ibn 'Abbas: that some people from the people of shirk had killed and killed much, and committed adultery and committed much, then they came to Muhammad (ﷺ) and said: "What you say and call to is indeed good; if only you would inform us that there is an expiation for what we have done." So there was revealed: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾, and there was revealed: ﴿Say: O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah; indeed, Allah forgives all sins; indeed, He is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ [al-Zumar: 53].

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu Fakhitah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah forbids you to worship the created and to abandon the Creator, and He forbids you to kill your child and feed your dog, and He forbids you to commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Sufyan said: This is His saying: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, and do not commit adultery﴾ (al-Suyuti mentioned it in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/277) and attributed it to Ibn Abi Hatim. It appears there as "from Abu Qatadah"; if that is so it is connected (mawsul), but if it is as stated here, it is mursal, and I have not clarified which of the two is correct, Allah knows best).

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that he said: "Athaman" is a valley in Hell.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means valleys in Hell in which adulterers are punished. The same was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

Qatadah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means a punishment. We used to narrate that it is a valley in Hell.

It has been mentioned to us that Luqman used to say: "O my son, beware of adultery, for its beginning is fear and its end is regret."

It has also appeared in the hadith narrated by Ibn Jarir and others, from Abu Umamah al-Bahili – both mawquf and marfu' – that "Ghayy" and "Athaman" are two wells at the bottom of Hell (Tafsir al-Tabari (19/29)). May Allah save us from them by His bounty and generosity.

Al-Suddi said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾: a recompense.

This is more apparent in the verse's outward meaning; for this reason it is explained by what follows it as a substitute: His saying: ﴿the punishment will be doubled for him on the Day of Resurrection﴾, meaning it will be repeated upon him and made more severe, ﴿and he will abide therein in humiliation﴾, meaning abased and degraded.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds﴾ – meaning: his recompense for what he did of these ugly attributes is what has been mentioned, ﴿except one who repents﴾ in this world to Allah from all of that, for indeed Allah accepts his repentance.

In this is evidence for the validity of the repentance of the murderer. There is no contradiction between this and the verse of an-Nisa': ﴿And whoever kills a believer intentionally, his recompense is Hell, abiding therein; and Allah will be angry with him and curse him and prepare for him a great punishment﴾ [an-Nisa': 93]. For although this is Medinan, it is unrestricted, so it is understood as applying to one who does not repent, since that one is restricted by repentance. Then Allah the Exalted has said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not forgive that partners be associated with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills﴾ [an-Nisa': 48, 116].

The authentic Sunnah has established, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the validity of the repentance of the murderer, as is mentioned confirmed in the story of the one who killed one hundred men and then repented, and it was accepted from him, along with other hadiths.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾: regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ there are two opinions.

The first: that they are substituted, in place of performing evil deeds, with performing good deeds. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ that he said: They are the believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; then Allah turned away from that concerning them and transferred them to good deeds, replacing evil deeds with good deeds for them.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite, at this verse, the lines:

"They were changed after their heat into autumn, and after the long breath, the panting."

meaning: those states were changed into other states.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: This is in this world: a man is in an ugly condition, then Allah replaces it for him with something better.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He replaced for them the worship of idols with the worship of Allah; and He replaced for them fighting the Muslims with fighting alongside the Muslims against the polytheists; and He replaced for them marrying polytheist women with marrying believing women.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah replaced for them evil action with righteous action, shirk with sincerity, immorality with chastity, and disbelief with Islam.

This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, and a group of others.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed by sincere repentance itself into good deeds; and this is only because whenever he recalls what has passed, he regrets, seeks forgiveness and asks for forgiveness, so the sin becomes an act of obedience in this respect. On the Day of Resurrection, even if he finds it written against him, it will not harm him, and it will turn into a good deed in his record, as the Sunnah has established regarding this, and the narrations transmitted from the early generations (salaf), may Allah have mercy on them, have been authenticated with it. This is the context of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise: a man will be brought and it will be said: Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones. It will be said to him: 'On such and such a day you did such and such, and on such and such a day you did such and such?' He will say: 'Yes' – he cannot deny any of it – and it will be said: 'For you, for every evil deed there is a good deed.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things which I do not see here.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed. Muslim alone narrated it (al-Musnad (5/170) and Sahih Muslim, no. (190)).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam sleeps, the angel says to the devil: 'Give me your record.' He gives it to him, and whatever good deed he finds in his record, he erases ten evil deeds from the devil's record and writes them as good deeds. So when one of you wants to sleep, let him say Allahu Akbar thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-four times, and glorify Allah thirty-three times – that is one hundred" (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/296); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/121): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, who is weak," and his hearing from his father is also not established).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah and 'Arim narrated to us, both said: Thabit – meaning Ibn Yazid Abu Zayd – narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman who said: A man will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection and will read its top; there are his evil deeds, and when his assessment nearly turns bad, he looks at its bottom and there are his good deeds; then he looks again at its top and behold, it has been changed into good deeds.

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abu al-Anbas narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will surely bring forth people on the Day of Resurrection who thought they had accumulated many misdeeds." It was said: "Who are they, O Abu Hurayrah?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah will replace with good deeds."

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Dayf, who was one of the companions of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise in four categories: the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), then the grateful (al-shakirin), then those who fear (al-khaifin), then the companions of the right hand (ashab al-yamin)." I said: "Why were they called the companions of the right hand?" He said: "Because they did good deeds and evil deeds. Their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will read their evil deeds letter by letter. They will say: 'O our Lord, these are our evil deeds, so where are our good deeds?' At that moment Allah will erase the evil deeds and turn them into good deeds. Then they will say: ﴿Here, read my book!﴾ [69:19]. They are the majority of the people of Paradise."

Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin said regarding ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾: "This is in the Hereafter."

Makhul said: "He will forgive them and make them good deeds." [Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both of these, and Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abu Jabir narrated to us, that he heard Makhul narrating, who said: "An old man, very aged, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man who betrayed and committed immorality, leaving no need or small matter without seizing it with his right hand. If his sin were divided among the people of the earth, it would destroy them. Is there repentance for him?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: 'Have you embraced Islam?' He said: 'As for me, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed Allah will forgive you for what you did before, and will replace your evil deeds with good deeds.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and my betrayals and my immoralities?' He said: 'And your betrayals and your immoralities.' Then the man turned away, saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' and 'Allahu akbar'."

[Ahmad al-Imam connected this in his Musnad (4/384) through the route of Nuh ibn Qays, from Ashath ibn Jabir al-Hudani, from Makhul, from Amr ibn Absah, with it being marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), abridged at its beginning and end. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/32): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that it is a narration of Makhul from Amr ibn Absah, so I do not know whether he heard it from him or not."]

Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu Farwah (Shatab), that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What do you say about a man who committed all sins and left no need or small matter? Is there repentance for him?" He said: "Have you embraced Islam?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then do the good deeds, and leave the evil deeds, and Allah will turn them all into good deeds for you." He said: "And my betrayals and my immoralities?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he kept saying 'Allahu akbar' until he disappeared from view."

[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/314); al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (3/352) through the route of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi, from Abu al-Mughirah with the same chain. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: "Other than Muhammad ibn Harun narrated this hadith from Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ..., (tawil shatab al-mamdud), and I think Muhammad ibn Harun made a mistake in it, and the correct version is what others have said."]

It was also narrated by al-Tabarani through the route of Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, from Yasin al-Zayyat, from Abu Salamah al-Himsi, from Yahya ibn Jabir, from Salamah ibn Nufayl, as a marfu' hadith. [Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/53). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Yasin al-Zayyat, who narrates fabricated (mawdu'at) reports."]

And he also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Isa ibn Shu'ayb ibn Thawban narrated to us, from Fulayh al-Shammas, from Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A woman came to me and said: 'Is there repentance for me? I committed fornication, gave birth, and killed the child.' I said: 'No, and may the eye not be pleased, and there is no honor for you.' So she stood up, calling out in grief. Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and I related to him what the woman had said and what I had said to her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Evil is what you said! Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah...﴾ up to His words: ﴿except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [25:68–70]?' So I recited it to her. Then she fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me.'"

This is a strange hadith (gharib) through this route, and among its narrators is one who is not known; and Allah knows best. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami with his chain, in similar wording, and in his version: "She went out calling in grief and saying: 'Alas for my grief! Was this beauty created for the Fire?' In his version also, when he returned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he searched for her in all the houses of Madinah and did not find her. When the following night came, she came to him, and he informed her of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to him. She fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me and repentance from what I did.' She freed a slave girl who was with her, and her daughter, and she repented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/27); Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/279), and al-Suyuti said: "Its chain is weak."]

Then He, exalted is He, said, informing about the comprehensiveness of His mercy toward His servants, and that whoever among them turns to Him in repentance, He will accept his repentance, regardless of what sin it was, whether grave or trivial, great or small: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, then indeed he turns to Allah with a true turning﴾ [25:71], meaning: indeed Allah accepts his repentance, just as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [4:110]; and He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charity, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾ [9:104]; and He said: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [39:53], meaning: for whoever repents to Him.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 68–71 (part 1 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from Shaqiq, from 'Abdullah – that is, Ibn Mas'ud – who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was asked: "Which sin is the greatest?" He said: "That you set up a rival (nidd) to Allah while He created you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you kill your child fearing that it will eat with you." He said: "Then which?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." 'Abdullah said: And Allah revealed as confirmation of that: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god, and do not kill the soul which Allah has forbidden, except by right, and do not commit adultery – and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾.

Al-Nasa'i narrated it likewise from Hannad ibn al-Sari, from Abu Mu'awiyah, with the same chain (al-Musnad (1/380) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11368)).

It was also narrated by al-Bukhari and Muslim, from the hadith of al-A'mash and Mansur – al-Bukhari added: and Wasil – all three from Abu Wa'il, Shaqiq ibn Salamah, from Abu Maysarah 'Amr ibn Shurahbil, from Ibn Mas'ud, with the same (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)). Allah knows best. The wording of both on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud is: He said: I said: "O Messenger of Allah, which sin is greatest?" – and the hadith continues.

A gharib route: Ibn Jarir said: Ahmad ibn Ishaq al-Ahwazi narrated to us, 'Amir ibn Mudrik narrated to us, al-Sari – meaning Ibn Isma'il – narrated to us, al-Sha'bi narrated to us, from Masruq who said: 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) went out one day and I followed him. He sat on a raised ground, and I sat below him, my face level with his knees. I seized the opportunity of his solitude and said: "May my father and mother be ransomed for you, O Messenger of Allah, which of the sins is greatest?" He said: "That you call upon a rival to Allah while He created you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you kill your child out of fear that it will eat with you." I said: "Then what?" He said: "That you commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." Then he recited: ﴿And those who do not invoke with Allah another god﴾ to the end of the verse (Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (6811) and Sahih Muslim, no. (86)).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Ibn Abi 'Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from 'Amr, from Abu Fakhitah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to a man: "Allah forbids you to worship the created and to abandon the Creator, and He forbids you to kill your child and feed your dog, and He forbids you to commit adultery with your neighbour's wife." * *

As for His saying: ﴿and whoever does that will meet a penalty﴾: it is narrated from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr that he said: "Athaman" is a valley in Hell.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿will meet a penalty﴾ means valleys in Hell in which adulterers are punished. The same was narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿except one who repents and believes and does righteous deeds﴾ – meaning: his recompense for what he did of these ugly attributes is what has been mentioned, ﴿except one who repents﴾ in this world to Allah from all of that, for indeed Allah accepts his repentance.
