* *

As for His saying: ﴿those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds, and ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾: regarding the meaning of His saying ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ there are two opinions.

The first: that they are substituted, in place of performing evil deeds, with performing good deeds. 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Those – Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ that he said: They are the believers who, before their faith, were upon evil deeds; then Allah turned away from that concerning them and transferred them to good deeds, replacing evil deeds with good deeds for them.

Mujahid narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he used to recite, at this verse, the lines:

"They were changed after their heat into autumn, and after the long breath, the panting."

meaning: those states were changed into other states.

'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: This is in this world: a man is in an ugly condition, then Allah replaces it for him with something better.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: He replaced for them the worship of idols with the worship of Allah; and He replaced for them fighting the Muslims with fighting alongside the Muslims against the polytheists; and He replaced for them marrying polytheist women with marrying believing women.

al-Hasan al-Basri said: Allah replaced for them evil action with righteous action, shirk with sincerity, immorality with chastity, and disbelief with Islam.

This is the view of Abu al-'Aliyah, Qatadah, and a group of others.

The second opinion: that those past evil deeds are transformed by sincere repentance itself into good deeds; and this is only because whenever he recalls what has passed, he regrets, seeks forgiveness and asks for forgiveness, so the sin becomes an act of obedience in this respect. On the Day of Resurrection, even if he finds it written against him, it will not harm him, and it will turn into a good deed in his record, as the Sunnah has established regarding this, and the narrations transmitted from the early generations (salaf), may Allah have mercy on them, have been authenticated with it. This is the context of the hadith. Imam Ahmad said:

Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, from al-Ma'rur ibn Suwayd, from Abu Dharr, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed I know the last of the people of the Fire to leave the Fire, and the last of the people of Paradise to enter Paradise: a man will be brought and it will be said: Set aside his major sins and question him about his minor ones. It will be said to him: 'On such and such a day you did such and such, and on such and such a day you did such and such?' He will say: 'Yes' – he cannot deny any of it – and it will be said: 'For you, for every evil deed there is a good deed.' He will say: 'O Lord, I did things which I do not see here.'" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) laughed until his molars showed. Muslim alone narrated it (al-Musnad (5/170) and Sahih Muslim, no. (190)).

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: Hashim ibn Yazid narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il narrated to us, my father narrated to me, Damdam ibn Zur'ah narrated to me, from Shurayh ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu Malik al-Ash'ari who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When the son of Adam sleeps, the angel says to the devil: 'Give me your record.' He gives it to him, and whatever good deed he finds in his record, he erases ten evil deeds from the devil's record and writes them as good deeds. So when one of you wants to sleep, let him say Allahu Akbar thirty-three times, praise Allah thirty-four times, and glorify Allah thirty-three times – that is one hundred" (al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/296); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/121): "In it is Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash, who is weak," and his hearing from his father is also not established).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Abu Salamah and 'Arim narrated to us, both said: Thabit – meaning Ibn Yazid Abu Zayd – narrated to us, 'Asim narrated to us, from Abu 'Uthman, from Salman who said: A man will be given his record on the Day of Resurrection and will read its top; there are his evil deeds, and when his assessment nearly turns bad, he looks at its bottom and there are his good deeds; then he looks again at its top and behold, it has been changed into good deeds.

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Musa al-Zuhri Abu Dawud narrated to us, Abu al-Anbas narrated to us, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: "Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will surely bring forth people on the Day of Resurrection who thought they had accumulated many misdeeds." It was said: "Who are they, O Abu Hurayrah?" He said: "Those whose evil deeds Allah will replace with good deeds."

And he also said: Abi narrated to us, Abd Allah ibn Abi Ziyad narrated to us, Sayyar narrated to us, Ja'far narrated to us, Abu Hamzah narrated to us, from Abu al-Dayf, who was one of the companions of Mu'adh ibn Jabal, who said: "The people of Paradise will enter Paradise in four categories: the God-fearing (al-muttaqin), then the grateful (al-shakirin), then those who fear (al-khaifin), then the companions of the right hand (ashab al-yamin)." I said: "Why were they called the companions of the right hand?" He said: "Because they did good deeds and evil deeds. Their books will be given to them in their right hands, and they will read their evil deeds letter by letter. They will say: 'O our Lord, these are our evil deeds, so where are our good deeds?' At that moment Allah will erase the evil deeds and turn them into good deeds. Then they will say: ﴿Here, read my book!﴾ [69:19]. They are the majority of the people of Paradise."

Ali ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-Abidin said regarding ﴿Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾: "This is in the Hereafter."

Makhul said: "He will forgive them and make them good deeds." [Ibn Abi Hatim narrated both of these, and Ibn Jarir narrated the like of it from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab.]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abi narrated to us, Muhammad ibn al-Wazir al-Dimashqi narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim narrated to us, Abu Jabir narrated to us, that he heard Makhul narrating, who said: "An old man, very aged, whose eyebrows had fallen over his eyes, came and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, a man who betrayed and committed immorality, leaving no need or small matter without seizing it with his right hand. If his sin were divided among the people of the earth, it would destroy them. Is there repentance for him?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: 'Have you embraced Islam?' He said: 'As for me, I bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and Messenger.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Indeed Allah will forgive you for what you did before, and will replace your evil deeds with good deeds.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, and my betrayals and my immoralities?' He said: 'And your betrayals and your immoralities.' Then the man turned away, saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' and 'Allahu akbar'."

[Ahmad al-Imam connected this in his Musnad (4/384) through the route of Nuh ibn Qays, from Ashath ibn Jabir al-Hudani, from Makhul, from Amr ibn Absah, with it being marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ), abridged at its beginning and end. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/32): "Its narrators are trustworthy, except that it is a narration of Makhul from Amr ibn Absah, so I do not know whether he heard it from him or not."]

Al-Tabarani narrated from the hadith of Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan ibn Amr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, from Abu Farwah (Shatab), that he came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "What do you say about a man who committed all sins and left no need or small matter? Is there repentance for him?" He said: "Have you embraced Islam?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then do the good deeds, and leave the evil deeds, and Allah will turn them all into good deeds for you." He said: "And my betrayals and my immoralities?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Then he kept saying 'Allahu akbar' until he disappeared from view."

[Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/314); al-Khatib narrated it in Tarikh Baghdad (3/352) through the route of Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, from Muhammad ibn Harun al-Harbi, from Abu al-Mughirah with the same chain. Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: "Other than Muhammad ibn Harun narrated this hadith from Abu al-Mughirah, from Safwan, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr, that a man came to the Prophet ﷺ..., (tawil shatab al-mamdud), and I think Muhammad ibn Harun made a mistake in it, and the correct version is what others have said."]

It was also narrated by al-Tabarani through the route of Abu Farwah al-Rahawi, from Yasin al-Zayyat, from Abu Salamah al-Himsi, from Yahya ibn Jabir, from Salamah ibn Nufayl, as a marfu' hadith. [Al-Tabarani, al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (7/53). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (1/31): "In its chain is Yasin al-Zayyat, who narrates fabricated (mawdu'at) reports."]

And he also said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us, Isa ibn Shu'ayb ibn Thawban narrated to us, from Fulayh al-Shammas, from Ubayd ibn Abi Ubayd, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "A woman came to me and said: 'Is there repentance for me? I committed fornication, gave birth, and killed the child.' I said: 'No, and may the eye not be pleased, and there is no honor for you.' So she stood up, calling out in grief. Then I prayed the dawn prayer with the Prophet ﷺ, and I related to him what the woman had said and what I had said to her. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Evil is what you said! Did you not read this verse: ﴿And those who do not call upon another god with Allah...﴾ up to His words: ﴿except one who repents, believes, and does righteous work; for those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [25:68–70]?' So I recited it to her. Then she fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me.'"

This is a strange hadith (gharib) through this route, and among its narrators is one who is not known; and Allah knows best. Ibn Jarir narrated it from the hadith of Ibrahim ibn al-Mundhir al-Hizami with his chain, in similar wording, and in his version: "She went out calling in grief and saying: 'Alas for my grief! Was this beauty created for the Fire?' In his version also, when he returned from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, he searched for her in all the houses of Madinah and did not find her. When the following night came, she came to him, and he informed her of what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had said to him. She fell into prostration and said: 'Praise be to Allah, who has made a way out for me and repentance from what I did.' She freed a slave girl who was with her, and her daughter, and she repented to Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [Tafsir al-Tabari (19/27); Ibn Mardawayh narrated it, as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/279), and al-Suyuti said: "Its chain is weak."]

Then He, exalted is He, said, informing about the comprehensiveness of His mercy toward His servants, and that whoever among them turns to Him in repentance, He will accept his repentance, regardless of what sin it was, whether grave or trivial, great or small: ﴿And whoever repents and does righteous work, then indeed he turns to Allah with a true turning﴾ [25:71], meaning: indeed Allah accepts his repentance, just as He said, exalted is He: ﴿And whoever does wrong or wrongs himself and then seeks forgiveness of Allah will find Allah Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [4:110]; and He said: ﴿Do they not know that Allah is the One who accepts repentance from His servants and takes charity, and that Allah is the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful?﴾ [9:104]; and He said: ﴿Say, "O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of Allah. Indeed, Allah forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful"﴾ [39:53], meaning: for whoever repents to Him.

This is also among the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful: they ﴿do not bear witness to falsehood﴾. It has been said that this means shirk and the worship of idols. It has also been said that it means lying, wickedness, vain talk, and falsehood.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: it means amusement and singing.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Tawus, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others said: it means the festivals of the polytheists.

'Amr ibn Qays said: it means evil gatherings and obscenity.

Malik reported from al-Zuhri: they do not attend the drinking of wine, nor do they desire it, as has come in the hadith: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table over which wine is passed around." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 2801, through the chain of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from Tawus from Jabir, traced to the Prophet. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we do not know from the hadith of Tawus from Jabir except through this route." He then cited the scholars' criticism of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym's weakness.)

It has also been said that the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿do not bear witness to falsehood﴾, is the testimony of falsehood, which is lying deliberately against another. This is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said it three times. We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He had been reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and false speech; beware, and false testimony; beware, and false speech and false testimony." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would be silent."

The more apparent meaning from the context is that the intended sense is: they do not bear witness to falsehood, that is, they do not attend it. This is why He said: ﴿and when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, and if they happen to pass by it, they pass on and are not soiled by anything from it. This is why He said: ﴿they pass by with dignity﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu al-Husayn al-'Ijli narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, Ibrahim ibn Maysarah informed me that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement and turned away, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Ibn Mas'ud has become dignified in the morning and in the evening."

And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Nahwi narrated to us, Hibban narrated to us, Abdullah informed us, Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, Ibn Maysarah informed me, saying: It reached me that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement, turning away, and did not stop. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ibn Mas'ud has become dignified in the morning and in the evening." Then Ibrahim ibn Maysarah recited: ﴿and when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾, these are also attributes of the believers: ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely﴾ (al-Anfal 2). This is in contrast to the disbelievers, for when they hear the speech of Allah it has no effect on them, and they do not refrain from what they were upon; rather they remain persistent in their disbelief, transgression, ignorance, and misguidance. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, some of them say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth upon their filth﴾ (al-Tawbah 124–125).

So His words ﴿they do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: unlike the disbeliever who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, and remains in his state as if he had not heard them, deaf and blind.

Mujahid said: His words ﴿they do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: they did not hear, did not see, and did not understand anything.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: How many a man reads them and falls down upon them deaf and blind!

Qatadah said: His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: they were not deaf to the truth nor blind to it. By Allah, they are a people who understood from Allah and benefited from what they heard of His Book.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Usayd ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Humran narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Sha'bi: "A man sees people prostrating but did not hear what they prostrated for; should he prostrate with them?" He recited this verse: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning: he should not prostrate with them, because he has not reflected on the matter of the prostration verse. The believer should not be a mere follower (imma'ah) but should act with insight into his affair and with clear and evident certainty.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes"﴾, meaning: those who ask Allah to bring forth from their loins and their offspring those who obey Him and worship Him alone, with no partner.

Ibn 'Abbas said: they mean one who acts in obedience, so that their eyes are comforted by him in this world and the Hereafter.

'Ikrimah said: they did not intend by this beauty or handsomeness, but they intended that they would be obedient.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, when asked about this verse, said: It is that Allah shows the Muslim servant obedience to Him in his wife, his brother, and his close relative. By Allah, nothing comforts the eye of a Muslim more than to see a child, or a grandchild, or a brother, or a close relative, obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Juraij said concerning His words, ﴿grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes﴾: "They worship You and perfect their worship of You, and they do not draw upon us misdeeds."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning: they ask Allah for their spouses and offspring that He guide them to Islam.

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'mar ibn Bishr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated to me, from his father, who said: One day we sat with al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and a man passed by him and said: "Blessed are these two eyes that saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! We wish we had seen what you saw and witnessed what you witnessed." Al-Miqdad became angry. I began to wonder, for he had said nothing but good! Then he turned toward him and said: "What moves a man to wish for a presence that Allah has kept him from? He does not know how he would have been in it if he had witnessed it! By Allah, there were people who were present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom Allah threw on their faces into the Fire, who did not respond to him and did not believe him. Do you not praise Allah that He brought you out, knowing none but your Lord, believing in what your Prophet brought, after you have been spared the trial through others? Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ at the most severe state in which He sent any prophet, during a gap in ignorance, when they saw no religion better than the worship of idols. So he came with a Criterion (Furqan) by which he distinguished between truth and falsehood, and separated the father from his son, so that a man would see his father or son or brother as a disbeliever, while Allah had opened the lock of his heart to faith, knowing that if that one dies he will enter the Fire, so his eye would not be comforted while he knows his beloved is in the Fire. This is the comfort that Allah the Exalted spoke of: ﴿And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes'﴾." This is a sound chain, though they did not record it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And make us a leader for the God-fearing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: leaders whom they are followed by in good.

Others said: guides who are themselves guided, and callers to good. So they loved that their worship be connected to the worship of their children and offspring, and that their guidance extend to others for their benefit. That is greater in reward and better in final return. This is why it has come in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, knowledge from which others benefit after him, or ongoing charity."

So he came with a Criterion (Furqan) by which he distinguished between truth and falsehood, and separated the father from his son, so that a man would see his father or son or brother as a disbeliever, while Allah had opened the lock of his heart to faith, knowing that if that one dies he will enter the Fire, so his eye would not be comforted while he knows his beloved is in the Fire. This is the comfort that Allah the Exalted spoke of: ﴿And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes'﴾." This is a sound chain, though they did not record it.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And make us a leader for the God-fearing﴾. Ibn 'Abbas, al-Hasan, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and al-Rabi' ibn Anas said: leaders whom they are followed by in good.

Others said: guides who are themselves guided, and callers to good. So they loved that their worship be connected to the worship of their children and offspring, and that their guidance extend to others for their benefit. That is greater in reward and better in final return. This is why it has come in Sahih Muslim, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When the son of Adam dies, his deeds are cut off except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, knowledge from which others benefit after him, or ongoing charity."

This is also among the attributes of the servants of the Most Merciful: they ﴿do not bear witness to falsehood﴾. It has been said that this means shirk and the worship of idols. It has also been said that it means lying, wickedness, vain talk, and falsehood.

Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyyah said: it means amusement and singing.

Abu al-'Aliyah, Tawus, Muhammad ibn Sirin, al-Dahhak, al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and others said: it means the festivals of the polytheists.

'Amr ibn Qays said: it means evil gatherings and obscenity.

Malik reported from al-Zuhri: they do not attend the drinking of wine, nor do they desire it, as has come in the hadith: "Whoever believes in Allah and the Last Day, let him not sit at a table over which wine is passed around." (Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. 2801, through the chain of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym from Tawus from Jabir, traced to the Prophet. al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith, which we do not know from the hadith of Tawus from Jabir except through this route." He then cited the scholars' criticism of Layth ibn Abi Sulaym's weakness.)

It has also been said that the meaning of the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿do not bear witness to falsehood﴾, is the testimony of falsehood, which is lying deliberately against another. This is established in the two Sahihs from Abu Bakrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shall I not inform you of the greatest of the major sins?" He said it three times. We said: "Yes, O Messenger of Allah." He said: "Associating partners with Allah, and disobedience to parents." He had been reclining, then he sat up and said: "Beware, and false speech; beware, and false testimony; beware, and false speech and false testimony." He kept repeating it until we said: "I wish he would be silent."

The more apparent meaning from the context is that the intended sense is: they do not bear witness to falsehood, that is, they do not attend it. This is why He said: ﴿and when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾, meaning they do not attend falsehood, and if they happen to pass by it, they pass on and are not soiled by anything from it. This is why He said: ﴿they pass by with dignity﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu al-Husayn al-'Ijli narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, Ibrahim ibn Maysarah informed me that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement and turned away, and the Prophet ﷺ said: "Ibn Mas'ud has become dignified in the morning and in the evening."

And al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Salamah al-Nahwi narrated to us, Hibban narrated to us, Abdullah informed us, Muhammad ibn Muslim informed us, Ibn Maysarah informed me, saying: It reached me that Ibn Mas'ud passed by a place of amusement, turning away, and did not stop. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Ibn Mas'ud has become dignified in the morning and in the evening." Then Ibrahim ibn Maysarah recited: ﴿and when they pass by vain talk, they pass by with dignity﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾, these are also attributes of the believers: ﴿those who, when Allah is mentioned, their hearts tremble, and when His verses are recited to them, they increase them in faith, and upon their Lord they rely﴾ (al-Anfal 2). This is in contrast to the disbelievers, for when they hear the speech of Allah it has no effect on them, and they do not refrain from what they were upon; rather they remain persistent in their disbelief, transgression, ignorance, and misguidance. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And whenever a surah is sent down, some of them say, "Which of you has had his faith increased by this?" As for those who believe, it has increased them in faith, and they rejoice. But as for those in whose hearts is a disease, it adds to their filth upon their filth﴾ (al-Tawbah 124–125).

So His words ﴿they do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: unlike the disbeliever who is reminded of the verses of his Lord, and remains in his state as if he had not heard them, deaf and blind.

Mujahid said: His words ﴿they do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: they did not hear, did not see, and did not understand anything.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: How many a man reads them and falls down upon them deaf and blind!

Qatadah said: His words, the Exalted: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾ mean: they were not deaf to the truth nor blind to it. By Allah, they are a people who understood from Allah and benefited from what they heard of His Book.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Usayd ibn 'Asim narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Humran narrated to us, Ibn 'Awn narrated to us, saying: I asked al-Sha'bi: "A man sees people prostrating but did not hear what they prostrated for; should he prostrate with them?" He recited this verse: ﴿And those who, when they are reminded of the verses of their Lord, do not fall down upon them deaf and blind﴾, meaning: he should not prostrate with them, because he has not reflected on the matter of the prostration verse. The believer should not be a mere follower (imma'ah) but should act with insight into his affair and with clear and evident certainty.

* *

As for His words: ﴿And those who say, "Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes"﴾, meaning: those who ask Allah to bring forth from their loins and their offspring those who obey Him and worship Him alone, with no partner.

Ibn 'Abbas said: they mean one who acts in obedience, so that their eyes are comforted by him in this world and the Hereafter.

'Ikrimah said: they did not intend by this beauty or handsomeness, but they intended that they would be obedient.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, when asked about this verse, said: It is that Allah shows the Muslim servant obedience to Him in his wife, his brother, and his close relative. By Allah, nothing comforts the eye of a Muslim more than to see a child, or a grandchild, or a brother, or a close relative, obedient to Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Ibn Juraij said concerning His words, ﴿grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes﴾: "They worship You and perfect their worship of You, and they do not draw upon us misdeeds."

Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: meaning: they ask Allah for their spouses and offspring that He guide them to Islam.

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'mar ibn Bishr narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Safwan ibn 'Amr informed us, Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr ibn Nufayr narrated to me, from his father, who said: One day we sat with al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, and a man passed by him and said: "Blessed are these two eyes that saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ! We wish we had seen what you saw and witnessed what you witnessed." Al-Miqdad became angry. I began to wonder, for he had said nothing but good! Then he turned toward him and said: "What moves a man to wish for a presence that Allah has kept him from? He does not know how he would have been in it if he had witnessed it! By Allah, there were people who were present with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ whom Allah threw on their faces into the Fire, who did not respond to him and did not believe him. Do you not praise Allah that He brought you out, knowing none but your Lord, believing in what your Prophet brought, after you have been spared the trial through others? Allah sent the Prophet ﷺ at the most severe state in which He sent any prophet, during a gap in ignorance, when they saw no religion better than the worship of idols. So he came with a Criterion (Furqan) by which he distinguished between truth and falsehood, and separated the father from his son, so that a man would see his father or son or brother as a disbeliever, while Allah had opened the lock of his heart to faith, knowing that if that one dies he will enter the Fire, so his eye would not be comforted while he knows his beloved is in the Fire. This is the comfort that Allah the Exalted spoke of: ﴿And those who say, 'Our Lord, grant us from our spouses and offspring comfort of the eyes'﴾." This is a sound chain, though they did not record it.

* *

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 25, verse 75–77:

When Allah, the Exalted, mentioned among the attributes of His believing servants what He mentioned of these beautiful qualities and noble deeds and statements, He said after all of that: ﴿Those will be rewarded﴾, meaning, those who possess these qualities, ﴿with the lofty chamber﴾, meaning on the Day of Resurrection, and it is Paradise.

Abu Ja'far al-Baqir, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Dahhak and al-Suddi said: it was so called because of its height.

﴿Because they were patient﴾, meaning, in upholding these things. ﴿And they will be met therein﴾, meaning in Paradise, ﴿with greetings and peace﴾, meaning they will be greeted first therein with salutation and honour, and they will receive reverence and esteem. So for them is peace, and upon them is peace, for the angels enter upon them from every gate: ﴿Peace be upon you, for what you patiently endured. And excellent is the final home.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning remaining, they will not depart, nor will they be moved, nor will they die, nor will they leave it, nor will they seek any change from it, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And as for those who were made happy, they will be in Paradise, abiding therein for as long as the heavens and the earth endure, except as your Lord wills — a gift uninterrupted.﴾ [Hud: 108]

* *

His saying: ﴿excellent as an abode and a station﴾, meaning excellent in appearance, and pleasant as a resting place and a dwelling.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication."﴾ meaning, He does not heed or concern Himself with you if you do not worship Him, for He only created creation so that they would worship Him, declare Him one, and glorify Him morning and evening.

Mujahid and Amr ibn Shu'ayb said: ﴿My Lord would not care for you﴾ means: what will My Lord do with you?

'Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Say: "My Lord would not care for you were it not for your supplication."﴾ He said: were it not for your faith. Allah informed the disbelievers that He has no need of them, since He did not create them as believers; and had He had need of them, He would have made faith beloved to them just as He made it beloved to the believers.

* *

His saying: ﴿So you have denied﴾, meaning, O disbelievers, ﴿so it will be inevitable﴾, meaning your denial will be inevitable for you, that is, it will necessitate your destruction, your punishment, and your annihilation in this world and the Hereafter. This includes the Day of Badr, as it was interpreted by 'Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatadah, al-Suddi, and others.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ﴿so it will be inevitable﴾ means: the Day of Resurrection. There is no contradiction between them. And Allah knows best.
